title: Supreme Court allows Trump administration to resume building border wall in Texas’s Big Bend
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Supreme Court cleared the way Monday for the Trump administration to resume border wall construction in the Big Bend region of Texas, a blow to bipartisan opponents who had argued the project is a waste of money that threatens the unique landscape.
The border wall is a signature project of President Donald Trump, who has long vowed to build a wall from the Pacific Ocean to the Gulf of Mexico.
Landowners and business owners in the Big Bend region, environmentalists and others who’ve opposed the construction project were bitterly disappointed with the court’s decision.
“This horrific decision clears the way for contractors to bulldoze pristine desert and dynamite canyon walls before the courts have even decided whether this destruction is legal,” said Laiken Jordahl, national public lands advocate at the Center for Biological Diversity, one of the groups that sued to stop the construction. “They’re signing off on the permanent destruction of the wildest place in Texas, and the theft of a great American river from all of us.”
Republicans in Congress last summer funded the project with $46 billion, and Customs and Border Protection has been rapidly erecting 12 miles of barriers a week across the entire border with a goal of eventually covering the entire 2,000-mile border with a mixture of 30-foot-tall steel walls, vehicle barriers and surveillance technology designed to stop illegal immigration and smuggling.
The government has pushed forward by issuing sweeping waivers to bypass regulations. Those rules are aimed at protecting the environment, but have historically slowed down major construction projects.
Big Bend residents of both parties oppose the project
In Texas’s Big Bend region, bipartisan opposition has rallied to fight back against the project, which would include 30-foot-tall steel walls in some areas as well as vehicle barriers and new roads.
They’ve argued that the barriers are a waste of money that threaten the local economy and lifestyle in an area of historically low illegal immigration. They say the job could be better done using only surveillance technology like drones.
A judge in Texas sided with opponents, finding that Congress likely had not clearly authorized such broad waivers for an area with the southern border’s lowest rate of migrant apprehensions. She ordered an immediate stop to all construction-related activity in the area, which includes Big Bend National Park as well as land up and down river in state and private hands.
The Trump administration filed an emergency appeal, saying there are illegal border crossings and drug seizures in Big Bend. More traffic could also be funneled there if there’s a gap in the wall, federal attorneys argued.
Customs and Border Protection head Rodney Scott said in an interview with The Associated Press that if the Big Bend area were left without a wall or other border infrastructure while other areas along the border get those fortifications, he’s convinced it would be swiftly overrun by cartels.
The Supreme Court agreed that the law sharply limits judges’ powers to intervene when the federal government decides speedy border barrier construction is necessary. The majority paused the lower court decision as the case plays out. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented.
CBP did not immediately respond to questions about how swiftly construction could restart. The agency started building an initial section of border wall in one area of the roughly 500-mile stretch that makes up the Big Bend region, but that was stopped with the judge’s order.
Construction activity in national park sparked outrage
The agency has encountered intense opposition from landowners up and down the region when it comes to getting permissions to enter their land to survey and build.
The Center for Biological Diversity sued over the construction, along with Friends of the Ruidosa Church and a river guide in the Big Bend area. Jordahl said it was the first time the government had waived a broad set of environmental laws inside a national park.
David Keller lives in the Big Bend region, is a member of the board of Conserve Big Bend and is a plaintiff in a separate lawsuit of landowners opposing the border wall projects.
He called the court’s decision devastating: “Everything is on the line again.”
Keller called the border infrastructure projects the “industrialization of one of the last best open undeveloped wild places in the lower 48 states.”
“We can’t afford to lose any more. Not an ounce. Not an acre,” he said. “We need wild country to be who we are, to be fully human, to be American I would say.”
The projects have drawn criticism from both Democrats and Republicans, including outgoing Republican Sen. John Cornyn of Texas, who wrote an op-ed arguing against the project published Monday in the San Antonio Express-News hours before the court’s decision.
“A combination of modern technology, adequate staffing, and meaningful cooperation with local officials and landowners offers a more sensible and effective path forward than indiscriminate construction of unnecessary barriers,” Cornyn wrote.
The government in August paused construction activity in Big Bend National Park that sparked outrage when bulldozers were spotted breaking ground in the park.
The government has repeatedly said no steel walls are planned for the national park. Initial plans included a new road as well as some vehicle barriers in the park. CBP has said in court filings that it will come forward with a finalized plan for what it intends to build in the national park but so far hasn’t done so while the case was at the Supreme Court.

title: VIDEO: Pilot rescued after emergency landing, marks third aviation incident in Florida within days
text:
VIDEO: Pilot rescued after emergency landing, marks third aviation incident in Florida within days
A pilot was rescued after a small plane made an emergency landing Sunday afternoon, marking the third aviation incident in Southwest Florida within a week.
Video from the Lee County Sheriff’s Office showed its aviation unit rescuing the male pilot from the aircraft that landed in a remote, landlocked area of the Estero Bay Preserve.
Officials said the area was inaccessible by boat or vehicle.
"A multi-agency response was quickly coordinated, and LCSO Aviation successfully conducted an aerial rescue, safely bringing the aircraft's sole occupant, to safety," the sheriff's office said in a post on Facebook.
Watch video of the rescue in the playfinder above
The pilot was evaluated and no injuries were reported.
Colton Novella, a Lee County resident who lives near the preserve, described the scene to Hearst sister station WBBH.
"I live maybe half a mile from there, and I actually saw all the firetrucks and, you know, rescue trucks going down there," Novella said.
When informed about the emergency landing, Novella expressed concerns about recent aviation incidents.
"There’s been so many plane crises lately, if you will. And it makes me think what the-- I mean, production-wise on these planes. You know what? What are they? What's missing? What-- what can they be cheapening out on?" Novella said.
The emergency landing on Sunday follows two other aviation incidents in the area.
On Saturday, a plane made an emergency landing in the middle of Bayshore Road in North Fort Myers. The plane was caught on video appearing to hit a pickup truck driving along the road.
Two pilots were inside the plane at the time of that incident. No injuries were reported.
Two days earlier, another plane crashed into a citrus farm in DeSoto County, Florida. The string of incidents has left many residents concerned.
"I don't know, that's insane that three times in one week someone needs to do something to fix it. For sure," Giuseppe Foglia, a Lee County resident, told WBBH.
Novella also shared his apprehension about flying after hearing about the recent events.
"Hearing about all these things, I'm like, maybe I'll start driving now when I have these big trips coming up, because I just, it makes me think what's going to happen in the commercial flight world next," Novella said.
The Federal Aviation Administration is now investigating the incidents.

title: Judge dismisses case from Dolly Parton’s manager alleging her nephew threatened her estate
text:
(AP) - A Tennessee judge on Monday dismissed a case brought by Dolly Parton ’s longtime manager who was seeking an injunction against her nephew and head of security, alleging he had threatened her estate and its employees.
The manager, Danny Nozell, asked for the dismissal on Thursday after the two sides came to an agreement. The order from Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles finalizes that request without prejudice, meaning it can be filed again.
Nozell, who runs She’s Alive, an entity founded to manage and protect Parton’s estate, had secured a temporary restraining order against Bryan Seaver and his security company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, in September.
The complaint seeking the temporary restraining order said Seaver had threatened violence and the destruction of Parton’s legacy and business empire. Nozell wanted to turn the order into a permanent injunction against Seaver. The two sides were to have publicly argued the claims on Tuesday.
Seaver’s lawyers said in a statement Monday that he “cares deeply about his Aunt Dolly, her music, her family, and the legacy she left behind.”
“He has made a career out of protecting his aunt while she was alive and remains committed to Dolly and his family” the statement said. “Mr. Seaver is grateful to put this misunderstanding behind him so that the entire family can continue to grieve peacefully and ensure that the bright light of Dolly’s legacy remains completely untouched.”
The dismissal brings a sudden and quiet end to a serious rift in the beloved country superstar’s inner circle that began while she was sick with cancer and spilled into public view in the weeks after her Aug. 25 death.
Neither side nor court documents have revealed anything about why the complaint was withdrawn, though one court filing said the sides had reached an agreement.
Emails requesting details and comment were sent to lawyers for Nozell and She’s Alive.
Seaver, who Parton had handpicked to announce her death, said in court filings that he considered Nozell a close friend and ally before the restraining order, and said the text messages Nozell cited as evidence of his threats were a “private conversation between two friends who were both frustrated, grieving and discussing strategy.”
Parton was a widely adored singer, songwriter, philanthropist and country music icon who rose from a log cabin in the Tennessee mountains to a stardom that spanned generations with songs including “Jolene,” “Coat of Many Colors,” “9 to 5” and “I Will Always Love You.” She also left behind a business empire, much of it based in her hometown, that employed many of her close friends and family.

title: Cooper Flagg records 43 points, 10 rebounds as Mavs rally past Pacers
text:
DALLAS — Newport native Cooper Flagg had 43 points and 10 rebounds and Kyrie Irving scored 35 while completing a back-to-back for the first time this season as the Dallas Mavericks rallied past the Indiana Pacers 125-122 on Monday night.
P.J. Washington Jr. could have extended the Dallas lead with four seconds left but missed both free throws, with Indiana’s Obi Toppin grabbing the rebound. The Pacers’ final possession ended with Dallas’ Caleb Martin tipping away a pass by Andrew Nembhard near the sideline.
Flagg had a season-high in scoring while Irving tied for his season best. They combined to score 26 points in the fourth quarter — including Dallas’ first 13 — as the Mavericks outscored the Pacers 35-29.
Irving, in action this season after missing 19 months with a torn ACL, played 28 minutes in Sunday night’s 130-93 rout of Brooklyn and a season-high 38 minutes against Indiana after sitting out the second game of the Mavericks’ first back-to-back 21 1/2 weeks ago. He hit a season-high seven 3-pointers.
Dallas (7-4) swept a three-game homestand and is three games over .500 for the first time since March 1, 2025 (at 32-29).
Flagg has four straight double-doubles and five this season.
The Pacers (3-8) were led by Pascal Siakam with 29 points, but only three of those were scored in the second half. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points with two of his four 3-pointers coming in the final minute.
Siakam hit 8 of 9 from the floor during the first half, including 5 of 6 behind the arc, plus 5 of 6 from the line for 26 points. He was the lone Pacer in double figures in building a 13-point lead that was 66-56 at halftime.
Up next
Pacers: Host Washington on Wednesday.
Mavericks: At Minnesota on Thursday.

title: Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky files resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Rep. Thomas Massie moved Monday to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing his fellow Republicans to remove one of the Trump administration’s most prominent figures following sweeping election losses blamed in part on fallout from the war in Iran.
Massie, a Kentucky Republican, read the impeachment resolution from the House floor just hours after it opened for the first day of sessions after the midterms. It largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Hegseth’s role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela.
The congressman, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Hegseth’s actions amounted to “high crimes and misdemeanors.”
Hegseth, he said, “knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders” and “remains a threat to the Constitution.”
President Donald Trump lashed out at Massie personally just hours after the congressman read the resolution, calling him a “loser” who “has a lot of hatred in his heart.”
A vote in the House could come by mid-week, but next steps are highly uncertain. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries supports the measure. If most Democrats follow him, Massie would only need support from a few Republicans to impeach Hegseth.
If the House votes to impeach, it would fall to to the Senate to either dismiss the charges or hold a trial. Republicans remain in the majority in both chambers, until the new Congress convenes in January with Democrats in control.
Sen. Chuck Schumer, the Democratic leader, endorsed the impeachment push. “Hegseth must stand trial before the Senate,” he said.
Republican leaders, who are eager to use their final weeks in power executing their own agenda, expressed frustration at the move. House Speaker Mike Johnson, who has tried to prevent the vote, said impeachment “in the middle of hostilities abroad would be a terrible, terrible look, a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see that.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he wasn’t sure why the vote was being held now.
“We’ll see what their ultimate decision is over there,” he said of the House. “We’ll have to deal with it accordingly here.”
Hegseth issues his own defense and prepares for a fight
Hegseth is stepping up his public statements ahead of the vote, telling reporters that he’s eager to defend the military actions that he and Trump have taken against Iran, Yemen’s Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela’s previous leaders.
After giving a speech at the Naval War College in Rhode Island, he brushed aside the impeachment push.
“There’s a lot of politically motivated people who may have substantial policy disagreements, but their disagreements are with success,” he told reporters. He added that “if we want to litigate” the military actions that the Trump administration has taken, “I’m happy to do it all day long.”
Asked about Vice President JD Vance blaming the Iran war for the massive GOP losses in the election, Hegseth noted that Trump said he would do it again, and “I agree.”
Hegseth also announced that he would hold a rare news conference on Tuesday — his first in over 180 days — on the impeachment threat.
Hegseth argued that the war was necessary because “someone had to confront the Iranian regime’s pursuit of a nuclear weapon” and said “the choice was don’t act and wish it away or take a bold move.”
Iran has long maintained that its nuclear program is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9 kilograms (972 pounds) of uranium that is enriched up to 60% purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90%.
Trump defended Hegseth to reporters on Monday, commending him for having “won the war” in Venezuela and “winning the war” in Iran, which continues to drag on.
Pentagon chief insists ‘Iran is devastated’
Hegseth reiterated that “Iran is devastated,” even though the Islamic Republic has been able to keep striking military bases in the Middle East that are used by the United States, causing billions of dollars in damage, as well as commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Disruptions to shipping in the waterway, where one-fifth of the world’s oil passed before the war, have led to higher energy prices that hit voters’ pocketbooks.
Hegseth’s defense of the war comes after about 6 in 10 voters said the U.S. made the “wrong decision” in taking military action against Iran, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of more than 100,000 voters in the United States.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended his fellow Cabinet secretary, saying that he believes Hegesth has been doing “a great job” and that its unfair that a Republican is pushing the impeachment effort.
“I work with him. And so I see perhaps a side of him that the media doesn’t see and members of Congress may not see,” Rubio told reporters at the Group of Seven industrialized democracies gathering in Paris. “But I think Pete works really hard. He’s incredibly smart.”
___
Associated Press writers Kevin Freking, Lisa Mascaro, Joey Cappelletti and Farnoush Amiri contributed to this report.

Judge denies three key motions in Lindsay Clancy case, clearing path for decision about second trial
text:
Judge denies three key motions in Lindsay Clancy case as second trial decision looms
Among the motions denied was one to dismiss charges in the deaths of Clancy's 3 kids
Judge denies three key motions in Lindsay Clancy case as second trial decision looms
Among the motions denied was one to dismiss charges in the deaths of Clancy's 3 kids
Three significant motions filed in connection with the case against Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three children, were denied on Monday by a superior court judge.
Judge William Sullivan of the Plymouth Superior Court heard arguments on all three of the motions last week. He issued his rulings on Monday:
- Sullivan denied without prejudice the prosecution's motion for a gag order, which would have blocked attorneys from speaking to the press about the case. He allowed the prosecution to renew the request "if circumstances change and it can demonstrate that a prior restraint is necessary."
- Sullivan denied a defense motion to dismiss the case on the grounds that retrying Clancy would constitute double jeopardy. He rejected the defense's argument that the lone holdout on the jury should have been replaced before a mistrial was declared.
- Sullivan also denied the defense request for an inquiry into the holdout juror, including allegations of lying on his questionnaire and using a cellphone while in the jury room. "Because Clancy has failed to demonstrate that the requested evidence is relevant and material to her defense at any retrial of the murder indictment, the Court declines to exercise its discretion to order production," Sullivan wrote. "Nor can the Court perceive any valid justification for examining Juror Doe under oath at this point in the proceedings."
Clancy, 36, was on trial over the summer for the deaths of 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan at their Duxbury home on Jan. 24, 2023. Her defense argued she was not criminally responsible for murder because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time of the killings.
The jury was ultimately deadlocked, with a reported 11-1 split in favor of acquittal after seven days of deliberations. A mistrial was declared.
Last week, when Sullivan asked the prosecutors whether they were planning to pursue another trial, Assistant District Attorney Jennifer Sprague replied, "We're not at that point yet."
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington, however, was more direct.
"I want a trial, and I want it with you, and I want it this spring," he told the judge.
Clancy's case is scheduled to return to court on Nov. 16, and District Attorney Tim Cruz said he would "be talking more" about the path forward after that hearing.

title: Sandwich shop coming to Westbrook
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
The owner of a popular local food truck plans to open a sandwich and grab-and-go meals restaurant in Westbrook this winter.
Owner Dan Perreault is launching Chums Sandwiches at 57 Bridge St., after Sumo Sushi and Grill completes its move to the former Portland Pie Company space on Main Street, as first reported by Portland Food Map. Perreault hopes to open in January, though his schedule depends on the timing of Sumo’s move.
Perreault also owns the Millside Creations food truck. He said the menu at Chums will include “variety store-style” sandwiches like Maine Italians, BLTs, pastrami and cheddar, egg, ham and chicken salads, and specialty items like “The Millworker,” a steak and Cooper cheese sub with bacon, grilled onions and Chums special sauce.
The grab-and-go selections will include breakfast sandwiches in the morning, and entrées like honey chicken over rice with fried vegetables, meatloaf with potatoes and gravy, American chop suey, shepherd’s pie and chef salads.
Perreault said the shop’s name was inspired by his late father, a passionate home cook, and the way his Franco-American family addresses kids as “Chum.”
Perreault expects the 24-seat restaurant will be open Monday-Saturday from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.

Crews make progress in containment of Wild River Fire in White Mountains
text:
Crews make progress in containment of Wild River Fire in White Mountain National Forest
Firefighters have been making significant progress on suppressing the Wild River Fire since it started last week in the White Mountain National Forest.
As of Sunday, the wildfire was 29% contained and burning a total of 821 acres. The containment and acreage totals remained the same in Monday's update from the U.S. Forest Service.
The Forest Service said the rain that happened over the weekend helped reduce fire activity, allowing crews to focus on securing containment lines, monitoring for hotspots and strengthening areas where fire could still become active under changing weather conditions.
As of Monday, the resources being used to fight the fire include two helicopters, two fire engines, eight suppression modules and an unmanned aerial system. The Forest Service said that 95 personnel were involved in the fire suppression operations.
The Wild River Fire was first reported the afternoon of Nov. 1, just southeast of Gorham, New Hampshire, and just south of Gilead, Maine, near Evans Notch.
On Wednesday, the Forest Service issued a closure order that remains in effect. Click here to see a map of the closure.
On Thursday, officials revealed that they believed the fire was caused by humans. A community meeting was held that evening to share information with people who live in the area and to answer questions.
Another public information meeting about the Wild River Fire is scheduled from 6 to 7 p.m. Tuesday at Shelburne Town Hall at 74 Village Road in Shelburne, New Hampshire. People can also attend the meeting virtually through Microsoft Teams. Click here for the Teams link for Tuesday's meeting.

title: ‘Catan’ Movie in the Works at Netflix
text:
A ‘Catan’ Movie Is in the Works at Netflix
Settle down, board game fans. Someone’s trying to make a Catan movie.
That someone is Netflix, which acquired the rights to the perennially best-selling board game in 2025. Per Deadline, they have brought in “Aaron and Adam Nee to write and direct a live-action movie based on the game.”
The Nee brothers do have at least some toy-to-movie adaptation experience. Their most recent credit was a gig co-writing the 2026 Masters of the Universe film from Amazon, based on the old He-Man action figure line from Mattel. Before that they wrote and directed the action rom-com The Lost City starring Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum.
READ MORE: The Best Movies Based on Toys
Catan — which was known for years in America as Settlers of Catan — is a German board game designed by Klaus Teuber. It was introduced in 1995 and steadily grew in popularity through the decades. It’s sold tens of millions of copies worldwide.
Here is how the official Catan website describes the game’s premise:
The women and men of your expedition build the first two settlements. Fortunately, the yet uninhabited land is rich in natural resources. You build roads and new settlements that eventually become cities. Will you succeed in gaining supremacy on Catan? Barter trade dominates the scene. Some resources you have in abundance, other resources are scarce. Ore for wool, brick for lumber - you trade according to what is needed for your current building projects. Proceed strategically! If you found your settlements in the right places and skillfully trade your resources, then the odds will be in your favor. But your opponents are smart too.
In addition to this film, Netflix holds the rights to develop other films and shows and even video games based on Catan. I would like to see a hidden camera show watching people play the original board game, and observing the sore losers (like me) as they get more and more frustrated the more they get beaten by better players (like my wife).

title: College Football Playoff doubles up, expands to 24 teams beginning next season
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
(AP) - College football will expand its playoff to 24 teams beginning next year in a move that resets decades of tradition surrounding a once all-important regular season and dumps conference championship showdowns that used to be among the sport’s marquee events.
The announcement from the College Football Playoff and ESPN on Monday made official a deal that’s been in the works for months. The network reported it would pay an additional $1.7 billion over five years on top of the original $7.8 billion contract that runs through the 2031 season.
The new format will grant the Power Four conference champions automatic spots and give one more to the best team from the Group of Six. But that slot and the other 19 will be decided by a selection committee that will serve as the latest set of decision makers in college football’s long history of polls and opinions having lasting impacts on teams’ fates.
Beginning next year, around 30% of college football’s 68 power-conference schools will have a chance to play for the title, drawing the CFP closer to the NFL, which allows 43% of its teams into the playoffs. It leaves behind the last vestiges of yesteryear, when between four and eight teams entered December with a legitimate shot to win it all.
It’s a seismic shift that even ESPN conceded comes with some question marks. The network pays billions to televise regular-season games that might — or might not — have more meaning under the new system.
“In all honesty, it’s impossible to know for sure,” ESPN senior vice president Nick Dawson said in a conference call.
The revenue generated from the playoff expansion will presumably make up for the estimated $345 million the Power Four conferences generated in TV money for their title games. ESPN would then not be on the hook for $140 million of the extra money due to cancellation of the title games, the network reported.
How an expanded CFP will work
The top eight seeds will receive first-round byes in the new format and the playoff will start on the second weekend in December, with the first two rounds of games on campus. The traditional Army-Navy game will be played on the first weekend in December, which used to be reserved for conference title games.
Both the Southeastern and Big Ten conferences, whose approval was needed to adopt this change, and their Power Four brethren — the Big 12 and Atlantic Coast Conference — are banking that most of the additional spots will go to their members so their second-tier teams will have new motivation to keep spending big in an era of NIL payments and $50 million football rosters.
“I think it will be healthy for teams like our current situation, building to try to get to that point,” said coach Barry Odom, who is trying to rebuild at Purdue.
The first final for the 24-team playoff remains set for Jan. 24, 2028, in New Orleans. Traditional bowl games will still host the quarterfinal and semifinal rounds.
As for the rest of the bowls, most of them operated or televised by ESPN: “No decisions have been made at this time,” Dawson said.
As part of the expansion, the CFP is requiring Power Four teams to play at least 10 regular-season games against conference foes, other Power Four opponents and Notre Dame. Group of Six teams will have to play 10 games against conference opponents.
In theory, these requirements will keep everyone in the same ballpark when it comes to strength of schedule, which figures to play a huge role in the selection committee’s considerations.
Special treatment vanishes for Notre Dame
Notre Dame didn’t receive any guarantees, the way it did this year when, if it’s ranked in the top 12 by the CFP for what will be the last year of the 12-team postseason, it will get a spot.
Coach Marcus Freeman said he looks at the change as a net positive, in part because a team like his can now presumably afford more than one loss, and in part because of the new scheduling requirements. Notre Dame is one of only two independents left in major college football.
“I don’t want this to be like March Madness and have 60-something teams making the playoff,” he said. “But the more opportunities we have to make the playoff, it helps us.”
The new schedule also guarantees two off weeks during a regular season that will begin the week before Labor Day.
A bigger playoff changes the nature of the college regular season
The move to 24 teams marks the second expansion of the playoff since it began in 2014 as a four-team affair. Right after it moved to 12 in 2024, most thought it would eventually max out at 16, which was the SEC’s preference.
But the Big Ten wanted to go bigger, while the SEC balked at that, concerned about the league title game — a property it invented in 1992 and made billions from over the decades — along with the marketability of CFP games featuring third- and fourth-place finishers in power conferences.
ESPN took care of the money problem. Now, the question is whether fans will embrace an NFL-style free-for-all that could include about one-third of the Power Four’s 68 teams, depending on what happens with Group of Six schools whose role in these big-money power grabs seems to diminish with every move.
It’s the latest change for a sport that, for decades, built its distinct character and generated controversy by leaning on media and coaching polls to hand out national titles.
Like then, critics see a risk in giving more power to a selection committee that hasn’t really mastered four- or 12-team brackets. The exclusion of Florida State in 2023 and Notre Dame last season stand out as the best examples, and the first rankings this season left people scratching their heads again.
Skeptics also view the expanded playoff as another dilution of what is largely seen as one of the most important regular seasons in sports, replacing potential matchups between, say, Alabama and Georgia in an SEC title game with a 13 seed vs. 20 seed game that would pit, say, Kentucky and South Carolina.
Fan reaction “certainly weighed into the decision,” Dawson said.
“Ultimately, we just need to make a spectacular playoff,” he said. “The CFP has a responsibility to our fans, they’re the lifeblood of college football. We owe them to make this great. That really is our intent.”
As Big Ten commissioner Tony Petitti argued from the beginning, a postseason that gives bubble teams hope and keeps others vying for home-field advantage or byes will bring more eyes — not fewer — to the end of a regular season that sometimes boils down to only three or four traditional rivalry games with meaning.
Of course, nobody can be certain how things will play out. The only sure thing is that college football will never look quite the same.
“If they think it’s a good thing for college football, then I’ve got to believe that this is the route we’re headed,” Wisconsin coach Luke Fickell said, “and we’re going to make it a great thing for college football.”
___

title: Know when to hunt deer, but if you can, spend more time in the wood
text:
Most deer hunters know the best time to be in the woods. However, deer don’t wear watches. They’re in the woods 24 hours a day, and every one of those daylight hours offers the potential for an interaction.
Behaviorally, deer are considered to be crepuscular, which is a fancy way of saying they’re most active around twilight. They may be actively feeding, or finishing their meal before heading off to bed. Either way, the first hour is typically the best hour of the morning for deer hunters.
Deer spend most of their day in bed (what a life). However, that first morning repose is sometimes more of a nap than a full commitment to leisure. Deer are also ruminants. They’ll feed fervently, then lie down and, like a cow, regurgitate and chew on a cud of food. This aids in the digestion of a diet that consists largely of coarse, woody browse in the fall and winter.
Once that task is complete, they may have a little extra space in their complex, four-chambered stomach to fill. An hour or so after the daylight flurry of activity has subsided, there might be a little more movement, as the deer “top off the tank” before seeking their daytime beds. This gives hunters a little more incentive to stay seated for at least the first two or three hours of daylight.
Around hour three, many hunters begin to grow cold, restless, hungry or all of the above. Some will head out of the woods and home to a second breakfast or off to work. Others opt for still-hunting or walking. Either way, the hunter’s movement often creates more deer movement as they inadvertently push deer from their beds. A second, similar increase in activity occurs as more hunters leave the woods for lunch.
In between those waves is another special period that occurs only during the rut. Does have bedded down, but the bucks are still on the prowl and must travel farther and wider to find what they seek. Ask any whitetail guide around the country, and they’ll tell you the best time to shoot a buck during the rut is between 10 a.m. and noon.
If there are doldrums in the deer hunter’s day, they occur over the next 2-3 hours. Natural deer movement is at a minimum. However, there’s still the chance of unnatural deer movement, and the odds increase as you move closer to the time hunters are returning for their afternoon hunt.
Moving from mid-to-late afternoon, daytime deer activity gradually increases as deer stir from their slumber and seek food to fill their now empty stomachs. Odds of intercepting a deer increase with each passing hour until you reach another peak that typically occurs just as the last light is fading.
If your time is limited, the best tactic is to pick peak periods like dawn and dusk. If you have more leeway in how you spend your day, don’t ignore the off hours. As a friend of mine once said, “The best time to be in the woods is when the season is open.”
Bob Humphrey is a freelance writer and Registered Maine Guide who lives in Pownal. He can be reached at: [email protected]

title: Former Celtics teammates Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum set to face off for first time
text:
PHILADELPHIA — Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum — once anchors of an NBA championship team in Boston — haven’t made time to talk since the trade that ended their working relationship.
The former Celtics teammates have certainly had opportunities to catch up since Brown was traded to the rival 76ers in July for Paul George and draft picks.
They just don’t want to — and Brown and Tatum sure don’t plan to make small talk when the Celtics play Tuesday night in Philadelphia in the first matchup between the top two teams in the Eastern Conference.
“There’s nothing to talk about,” Brown said Sunday in Chicago. “He’s on his side; I’m on my side. Both of us are trying to win. Nothing to talk about. Check the ball up.”
The trade has been a success for both teams. The 76ers. with Brown and LeBron James aboard, are 9-2 and tied with the Lakers for the best record in the NBA.
The Celtics have the second-best record in the East at 8-2.
“I think it should be fun,” Brown said. “Never let a good opportunity for our team to show what we’re made of. I’m looking forward to it. Two heavyweights in the East. Let’s get it.”
Both stars are well aware the headlines and social media posts for this one are well beyond how both teams are playing on the court, or even how the Celtics blew a 3-1 series lead to Philadelphia in last season’s playoffs.
“It’s another game on the schedule,” Tatum said Sunday in Milwaukee. “It’s nothing more than Celtics versus Sixers.”
As for potential chitchat, Tatum said he’s “not able to tell the future.”
The trade busted up one of the league’s most successful 1-2 punches, after Brown and Tatum helped carry the Celtics to the 2024 NBA title.
Tatum missed most of last season while recovering from an Achilles tendon tear that happened during the 2025 playoffs, meaning Brown had to carry even more of the load for Boston — and he wound up with career-best averages of 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists.
Brown and Tatum’s off-court relationship was dissected throughout NBA media circles, and the question of whether they were more frenemies than friends could have strained their effectiveness this season in Boston.
Brown also seemed to feel underappreciated, a perception that only deepened when the Celtics included him in trade talks with Milwaukee when Giannis Antetokounmpo was on the market.
The Celtics instead stunned the NBA when Brown — the 2024 NBA Finals MVP and a five-time All-Star — was sent to the 76ers. When Brown got the call that Boston had traded him, he threw his phone across the room.
Brown said last month there was “ no beef ” between himself and Tatum, even as their squabbles dragged into the season.
“There might be a little lamb chops and some gravy,” Brown said last month in response to a social media post. “He should stay ready at all times.”
Brown took issue with Tatum saying in a video on his YouTube channel that he was “just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world” by Brown’s trade to the Philadelphia.
Brown responded on his Instagram account with a baseball cap emoji. “Cap” is slang for something that is not true. Asked if he had any response, Tatum sighed in October before expressing his frustrations with the entire situation for several minutes.
Both players have spoken glowingly about how they grew and thrived together during their nine years as teammates.
But the relationship has evolved since the Celtics chose Tatum as the player they wanted to build around after trading Brown in what amounted to a move to cut one of the two players with $300 million contracts from the payroll.
“I don’t have any animosity or beef, or ill will towards him,” Tatum said. “I think the toughest part is since he’s not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or the conversations haven’t been enough about what we accomplished — all the games we won, winning a championship, how we’ve grown together. It’s turned into this drama type of thing.”
Who doesn’t love a little drama in the NBA?
The game streams on Peacock and no doubt cameras and reporters will crowd the court ahead of the game trying to glean any interactions between the two stars.
Then the ball goes up. Brown said his feelings are in check.
“As of now, I’ve got no emotion toward nothing,” Brown said in Chicago.
He’s focused on leading the 76ers into NBA championship contention and a 2-1 road trip did nothing to dim the soaring expectations set for the franchise.
There are more good times ahead for Brown.
And none of them involve Tatum.
“I’m looking forward to our growth,” Brown said, “and we’ll get there.”

title: Neither voters nor Trump to blame for Collins’ loss
text:
Sen. Susan Collins now laments that she lost the election despite breaking with Trump, notably by voting once for impeachment. “It is never enough,” she is quoted as saying, offering that voters wanted tirades instead of results.
I fear that Sen. Collins is naive, in addition to calculating, as it seems obvious to voters like me that she and other Republican members of Congress have appeased Trump at our expense.
Collins voted more funding for ICE, despite its masked agents shooting and killing truly innocent people on our streets and terrifying thousands or millions of others. She voted to facilitate the passage of a bill cutting needed medical care and food to the poor, and driving our nearby hospital services to close. Collins provided key votes confirming judges who restrict women’s rights and empower one-person rule. And she voted to confirm the distorted and ill-informed Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. as head of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
How many more reasons do we need? Dare I use her campaign slogan? Thank you, Susan.

Portland

title: Monday Five and Five: From Championship Saturday to Winter Sports
text:
Monday Five and Five: A Gold Ball Comes Home and Winter Begins
That’s a wrap on the fall sports season.
And what a way to finish it.
Five Aroostook County soccer teams played for state championships Saturday, Wisdom brought home its first girls soccer Gold Ball, and four other County teams finished their seasons as state runners-up.
Normally, this is where the calendar would finally slow down.
Not this year.
Some basketball teams are already practicing, girls hockey is underway, postseason soccer honors are coming and the rest of the winter sports calendar isn’t far behind.
So for one final time this fall, here are my five from last week and five things I’m watching this week.
Five From Last Week
5. Madawaska Brings Home the Class D North Championship
Madawaska’s boys had one more big win left in them before heading to the state championship.
The Owls beat Fort Fairfield 2-0 in the Class D North final, with Aiden Gagnon and Josh Querze scoring first-half goals and Aleck Gendreau recording the shutout.
It was the third straight season Madawaska and Fort Fairfield met for the regional championship, and this time the Owls earned the trip south.
Madawaska’s season ended Saturday against Monmouth in the state final, but a Northern Maine championship and a state runner-up finish is still one heck of a season.
4. Fort Kent Girls Make It Four Straight
At this point, reaching the Class C North championship has become familiar territory for Fort Kent.
Winning it has too.
The Lady Warriors shut out Orono 3-0 to capture their fourth straight regional championship.
Reece Doucette scored twice, Hayden Plourde added another and Fort Kent’s defense kept Orono off the board.
That sent Fort Kent to its fourth consecutive state championship game before the Warriors finished as state runners-up against Maranacook.
3. Fort Kent Boys Win It in Overtime
The Fort Kent boys earned their trip to states in about as dramatic a way as possible.
Orono scored first, but Dominic Cyr answered for the Warriors before eventually getting another opportunity almost immediately after overtime began.
Cyr converted the penalty kick just 36 seconds into overtime, giving Fort Kent a 2-1 victory and the Class C North championship.
The Warriors then battled Hall-Dale in Saturday’s state championship before coming up just short, 1-0.
Regional champion. State runner-up. And one unforgettable overtime finish along the way.
2. Wisdom Boys Win a Wild Northern Maine Championship
If you were looking for one of the craziest games of championship week, Wisdom and Piscataquis delivered it.
The Pioneers won 5-4, with Cayden Hargrove scoring four times in the second half.
And somehow that still wasn’t the game-winner.
With just 13 seconds remaining, Zeke Cyr found the back of the net and sent Wisdom to the Eight-Player state championship.
The Pioneers eventually finished as state runners-up to Telstar, but that regional championship game is going to be remembered for a long time.
Four second-half goals from one player and a championship winner with 13 seconds left.
That’s tournament soccer.
1. Wisdom Girls Make History
There really wasn’t another choice for No. 1.
Wisdom’s girls are state champions for the first time in program history.
And they had to come from behind to do it.
Bangor Christian led 1-0 before Emma Soucy tied the game in the second half.
Then Ellie Cyr took over.
Cyr scored twice late, including the goal that put Wisdom ahead for good, as the Lady Pioneers rallied for a 3-1 victory right here in Presque Isle.
Mikayl Michaud made eight saves in goal.
It was also redemption in every sense of the word. Bangor Christian had beaten Wisdom twice during the regular season and defeated the Pioneers 3-0 in last year’s state championship.
This time, Wisdom got the final word.
A first Gold Ball for the program and one heck of a way to close the fall season.
Five to Watch This Week
5. The Rest of Winter Sports Are Almost Here
Enjoy the short break while it lasts.
Next Monday, November 16, practice begins for several more winter sports, including Classes A through D basketball, wrestling, indoor track, boys hockey and winter cheering. Wrestling, boys hockey, indoor track and cheering all list November 16 as their first practice date.
Skiing gets going a week later on November 23.
In other words, the quiet part of November isn’t going to last very long.
4. Girls Hockey Is Already Back
While most winter sports are still waiting, girls hockey has already started.
Practices opened November 2, with the first countable games beginning November 19.
That means hockey is already getting a head start while the rest of the winter calendar begins filling in around it.
3. Soccer Season Is Over, but the Honors Aren’t
The final whistles have blown, but we’re not quite finished talking about soccer.
The postseason honor season is next.
That means All-Aroostook selections will eventually enter the conversation, and I’ll also be working on something new of my own with The Rock to recognize some of the top boys and girls soccer players I watched and covered throughout the fall.
There were too many great performances this season to just close the book after Saturday.
2. It’s Time to Find Our Athletes of the Fall
Athlete of the Week is finished for the fall, but there’s still one more decision to make.
Who were the best boys and girls athletes of the entire season?
Soccer, cross country and golf gave us plenty of candidates, from state champions and regional champions to huge individual seasons and postseason performances.
This week we’ll start putting together the field for Athlete of the Fall, with separate boys and girls honors.
This one should be fun.
1. Basketball Starts Today
Yes, already.
Class S basketball teams are allowed to begin practice Monday, November 9, nearly a full week before Classes A through D get started.
That means several County programs are officially turning the page from fall to basketball today. On the girls side, the North-S division includes Ashland, Easton, Katahdin, Van Buren, Washburn and Wisdom.
Think about that for a second.
Wisdom won a state soccer championship Saturday.
By Monday, basketball season can begin.
That might be the best example possible of how quickly high school sports move around here.
And before long, gym lights, basketball sneakers and winter tournament talk will replace soccer fields and cold October sidelines.
From One Season to the Next
I’m not quite ready to completely close the book on this fall.
There were too many great games, great performances and stories worth recognizing before we move on.
But winter is coming quickly.
Basketball practices are starting, hockey is underway, more winter sports begin next week and we still have Athlete of the Fall and postseason soccer honors to work through.
The fall gave us plenty to remember.
Now we get ready to do it all over again.

text:
LYNN, Mass. (CNN) - After more than eight decades, the remains of a World War II veteran are finally home.
Pvt. Joseph Gala was laid to rest in Lynn, Massachusetts, on Thursday.
Gala, who was 21 when he died, entered the military in 1943 and was killed in action the following year in Burma.
His remains were classified as missing in action and remained that way for 82 years. However, DNA advancement helped officials identify his remains.
“And our family, mother, aunt, uncles, grandparents, I know they’re really happy,” Rose DiGregory, Gala’s niece, said.
A ceremony with full military honors was held in the World War II section of Pine Grove Cemetery.

title: Lobster trade group lauds US findings on whale endangerment
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
The Maine Lobstermen’s Association praised the federal government’s preliminary determination that deaths and injuries of endangered North Atlantic right whales attributable to U.S. fisheries was lower than previous estimates.
“They told us we had to make drastic changes or risk losing our fishery,” said Sonny Beal, the association’s chair. “We knew the government’s numbers didn’t add up.”
North Atlantic right whales are one of the world’s most at-risk species. Threats include entanglement in fishing gear, vessel strikes and climate change.
At the start of 2024, there were 384 right whales, according to the latest federal estimate.
New federal analysis
The National Marine Fisheries Service — which regulates the fisheries in federal waters, including Maine’s lobster harvesting — said last week that new scientific analyses indicate U.S. fisheries may be meeting the federal standard for protecting endangered North Atlantic right whales.
The analysis was a sea change from the government’s previous assessments, which found fixed-gear fisheries posed a threat to the endangered animal.
The latest analysis followed the association’s successful federal court challenge. In 2023, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit unanimously rejected the service’s evaluation of fishing impacts on right whales and required a reassessment.
In the latest preliminary analyses, the service indicated that estimates of fishing impacts might satisfy the federal “potential biological removal” standard, which is used to assess allowable human-caused mortality under the Marine Mammal Protection Act. The findings remain subject to scientific review.
Gear changes
For more than 25 years, Maine lobstermen have made substantial changes to their fishing practices to reduce the risk of right whale entanglement. Those include replacing floating groundlines with sinking rope, reducing vertical lines in the water, incorporating weak links and weak rope, marking fishing gear and complying with seasonal fishing restrictions. The measures have resulted in financial and operational costs for lobstermen.
Maine’s lobster industry is the nation’s most valuable fishery, accounts for roughly 75% of the value of Maine’s commercial fisheries and supports an estimated 17,500 jobs and $2 billion in economic activity.
A team of fishermen, scientists, conservationists and state and federal officials from Maine to Florida first published a plan to reduce death and injury to North Atlantic right, humpback and fin whales in 1997.
The plan has been modified on several occasions and today includes requirements such as use of weak links and sinking groundline, gear marking, seasonal area closures and a minimum number of traps per trawl.
In 2023, the federal government invested $82 million for technologies to reduce the risk of vessel strikes, increase the use of on-demand fishing gear and improve enforcement of federal regulations; and $17.2 million was allocated to the Maine Department of Marine Resources to improve data collection on the whale.
In 2024, another $6.9 million went to support the development of on-demand, or “ropeless,” fishing gear.
Over 85% of right whales have gotten tangled in fishing gear at least once in their lifetimes, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

title: 'I'm scared': Florida high school student swims through chest-deep floodwaters after bus drop-off
text:
'I'm scared': Student swims home through chest-deep floodwaters from school bus stop
A Florida high school student swam through chest-deep floodwaters after being dropped off by his school bus, sparking concerns from his father and criticism of the school district.
'I'm scared': Student swims home through chest-deep floodwaters from school bus stop
A Florida high school student swam through chest-deep floodwaters after being dropped off by his school bus, sparking concerns from his father and criticism of the school district.
A high school freshman in Port St. Lucie, Florida, swam through chest-deep floodwaters to get home after being dropped off by his school bus last Monday, a moment captured in a viral video that has raised concerns about the school district's response to the storm.
"I'm scared; I just wanted to get out of the water," Noah John said. "I was swimming. Like, it got way deeper to my chest when I hit the ditch."
Witness Martina Elieson, who filmed him swimming, described her reaction.
"I saw the children get off, and my heart sank," she said. "I was watching him. I'm disabled, but if he had gone down, I would've thrown my phone and went."
Noah's father, Romeo John, said he was "really shocked" when he saw the video.
The flooding began unexpectedly on Monday while students were at school. Romeo said neither he nor the school district anticipated the storm's magnitude.
"I went crazy the first time, because when he left early morning, 6 o'clock, we didn't know there was going to be a storm," he said.
As the skies opened, the district sent school buses to take students home. Noah described the conditions when he exited the bus: "The water was all the way up to the stairs. Every step had water on it." He added that the bus driver asked, "Do you want to get dropped off here?"
"I said, 'Sure.'"
Since the incident, Romeo has expressed concern about his son's health, noting that Noah has been unusually drowsy.
"My son right now, he shrugs," Romeo said.
Romeo also criticized the school district for poor communication during the flooding. He said he is glad that the video went viral so the whole country can see what happened.
During a news conference on Tuesday, the superintendent apologized to parents. Superintendent Jon Prince said the decision to keep schools open on Monday was made based on information from the Emergency Operations Center and the National Weather Service.
He called what happened "an unpredicted and unprecedented once in a century event for our community."
When asked for an interview, his office stated he was unavailable.

title: Credit counselor says stigma should not keep people from seeking debt help
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
(InvestigateTV) — People enrolled in Money Management International’s debt management plans now owe more than $1 billion in credit card and personal loan debt, the most the national nonprofit has seen in 13 years.
More than 60,000 people are enrolled. Many are putting everyday expenses such as groceries, gas and car repairs on credit cards as prices have jumped about 30% since 2019.
Ted Rossman, with Money Management International, said inflation, high interest rates and the rising cost of living are behind the numbers.
“The story behind the story is inflation, high-interest rates, just the rising cost of living that is really straining household budgets,” Rossman said. “And we’re going back to some unpleasant numbers that followed the financial crisis.”
Rossman said some households are clearly showing stress. Even for people who are working and getting raises, pay is often not enough right now to keep up with rising prices for gas, groceries, housing, medical bills and child care.
Rossman said people who are struggling should not wait to ask for help.
“Definitely speak up, ask for help, don’t be ashamed,” Rossman said. “There’s such a stigma around credit card debt, which I think is unfortunate. There’s this feeling that if you have credit card debt you did something irresponsible, right? A big vacation, shopping spree, no… in reality it’s usually practical things, it’s medical bills, it’s car repairs, it’s gas, it’s groceries, so take the shame out of it.”
Rossman said half of credit card holders carry debt from month to month, and the key is working to break the pattern. Options include connecting with a nonprofit credit counselor, taking out a personal loan or trying a zero percent balance transfer card to consolidate and pay down debt.

title: Cozy Maine skating spots for winter fun
text:
This winter, go all in on ice skating.
There are indoor rinks all around southern and central Maine where you can skate now, even before your local ponds and outdoor rinks are frozen over. There are also some covered rinks where the ice is maintained and skaters are protected from rain or snow.
Some of the indoor rinks are publicly owned or are part of a school or college. Some offer public skating sessions once a week, some almost every day. Some offer special events with music and strobe lights, or skating parties. At least one is free.
Here are some of the indoor or covered skating rinks around southern and central Maine, including, hopefully, one near you.
14 Pomerlau St., Biddeford. biddefordarena.com
This arena has hockey and figure skates available for rent for $5 during public skating sessions, though no pucks or sticks are allowed. Because the arena hosts a lot of hockey teams, public skating is limited and the schedule changes, so check the Facebook page for the latest information. The next scheduled public skating sessions are 11:30 a.m.-1 p.m. Nov. 11 and 6:30-7:50 p.m. Nov. 14. Admission is $5.
36 Hancock Drive, Bridgton. facebook.com
This school arena offers public skating as well as “stick and puck” sessions for hockey players. Hockey players must have their own equipment to participate and anyone under 18 must wear a hockey helmet with a cage. The cost for those sessions are $12. Admission for public skating sessions is $6 and skate rentals are $5. There are upcoming public skate sessions from 4-5 p.m. Nov. 15, 22 and 29 and stick and puck sessions from 5:10-6:10 p.m. Nov. 16, 23 and 30. The monthly schedule is posted on the arena’s Facebook page.
630 Pool St., Biddeford. une.edu
The NHL-size hockey arena here has seats for 900, so you can imagine yourself playing or performing for a crowd. There are open skate or stick and puck sessions (for hockey players) just about every day. On Friday at 9:15 p.m. and Saturday at 6:15 p.m., there will be “cosmic” public skating sessions, with neon lighting, music and a party atmosphere. But the schedules change and the university posts two-week schedules in a pdf on its website. The stick and puck is for skaters 18 and older and helmets with at least a half shield are required. Admission is $3 for children under 17 and $5 for adults. A limited number of rental skates are available for $3.
535 West St., Rockport. midcoastrec.org
This rink offers roller skating in the spring and summer and ice skating in the fall and winter. In November there are public skating sessions just about every day, usually in the early afternoon. There are also early morning “coffee club” skates at 8 a.m. on Wednesday and Friday. There are some stick and puck sessions on the monthly schedule, too. Admission is $8 for adults, $6 for people 60-plus and children 6-12, free for kids 5 and under. Rentals are $5.
985 Turner St., Auburn. norwaysavingsbankarena.com
At this arena, public skating sessions for November are scheduled for 3:50-4:50 p.m. on Sundays. Admission is $5 and skate rentals, in both youth and adult sizes, are $5. The public skating calendar is posted monthly on the arena’s website.
90 Acme Road, Brewer. penobscoticearena.com
This arena near Bangor offers a Frozen Friday Laser Light & Sound Skate from 7:30-9:30 p.m. on Fridays. Admission is $15 and skates can be rented for $5. The party-like events are so popular rink management recommends getting there 30 minutes early. There’s also a quieter Sunday afternoon public skate with no lights and soft music, plus other public skate sessions scheduled at various times. Admission for public skating is $10.
203 Whitten Road, Hallowell. maineicevault.com
Public skates sessions here are for people of all ages and abilities looking for a casual skate. Admission is $12 and skate rentals are $6. Weekend events often sell out, so the rink recommends purchasing advance tickets online. Memberships and discounted 10-packs are also available.
207 Thompson’s Point Road, Portland. thompsonspointrink.com
This popular outdoor rink is covered by an antique train shed roof. It’s located where the Thompson’s Point concerts are held in summer, with a view of the Fore River. The rink is slated to open for the season the weekend after Thanksgiving, with up-to-date schedules posted on the @thompsonspointrink Instagram page. There are daily public skating sessions, which are timed and ticketed. There are also skate rentals, training aids and skate sharpening services.
51 Main St., Kennebunk. kennebunkmaine.us
This open-side rink in downtown Kennebunk is free to all, all the time. Well, November through March, weather permitting. The roof comes down pretty low so the exposure to the outdoors is minimal. The rink is 60 feet by 90 feet and is open 8 a.m.-8 p.m. daily. The rink is town-owned and ice skating and other activities are supported by an endowment set up by town resident Geraldine Waterhouse and her granddaughter, Paige Hill.
225 Park Ave., Portland. portlandmaine.gov
Portland’s city-owned rink hosts hockey, events and public skating. There are public skating sessions just about every day in November, including 90-minute lunchtime sessions on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday and sessions from 1:30-3 p.m. Saturday and Sunday. The times vary from week to week so check the schedule on the website. No sticks or pucks allowed. Admission is $6 and skate rentals are $4.

title: How fake businesses can become a real problem for you
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
PHOENIX, Az. (InvestigateTV) — Imagine your name and home address are used to start a business, but you have nothing to do with it.
Morgan Johnson doesn’t own a furniture store or run a toy wholesaler, but there’s paperwork that sure makes it look like she does. Three times in the past year, someone has created limited liability companies in her name at her address.
Johnson discovered the fraud after receiving mail about pending credit accounts she never opened.
“I freaked out a little bit about it because it felt so intrusive,” she told On Your Side.
Fraudsters create fake LLCs with the goal of cashing in, often passing bad checks or opening a line of credit they’ll never repay.
“The bottom line is it’s not for a good reason,” said Tanya Gibson, the director of the Corporations Division at the Arizona Corporation Commission. “It’s a huge problem.”
According to data from the agency, the Corporations Division received 208 complaints about fake LLCs in September 2025. After a new system launched in early 2026, complaints dipped, but rose again to 180 in May 2026.
Why it’s easy to create a fake LLC
Currently, anyone can create an LLC online using only a name and address. No identification is required.
“We have no way to verify if that person has the ability to use an address,” said Gibson.
Gibson said she wants the law changed to give the division authority to validate information and deny filings if fraud is suspected.
In the meantime, changes are coming to make it tougher to file for fake LLCs. “[By July 1], we’re going to have our online ID verification, which will require a photo ID, front and back, and a selfie,” Gibson explained. “Then the software runs the information against multiple databases. You either come back verified or not. If you come back verified, you get a stamp on your account, and you’re free to file. If you are not verified for whatever reason, you will get a message saying that you need to come into the office to file.”
Gibson acknowledged the state cannot prevent fraud completely.
“We’re trying to throw as many hurdles in place as we can,” she said.
Once the state receives a complaint about a fake LLC, it can take months to get it dissolved. In the meantime, the division marks the status as pending inactive and not in good standing and flags it as undeliverable to alert banks and credit agencies.
Johnson said flagging fake LLCs isn’t enough.
“We need to do a lot more,” she said.
How to check for fraud
Fake LLCs could go unnoticed if victims don’t receive mail about them. Gibson said the agency often sees clusters of addresses, suggesting fraudsters are pulling lists of people and addresses at random.
Residents should check their own address for unauthorized LLCs and file a complaint with your secretary of state’s office.

By Kathryn Carley
Nov 9, 2026
A 2025 Congressional report found as a result of tariffs, the cost of five common items purchased for new babies, including car seats, cribs, strollers, high chairs and baby monitors, increased by 24%. (Adobe Stock)
Listen to this story HERE
Consumer advocates said families in New England continue to pay the high cost of tariffs on essential baby products, despite a September trade agreement between the U.S. and China meant to ease financial pressure.
The majority of domestically sold baby products are made in China and trade negotiators agreed tariffs should be relaxed on legally required car seats as well as toys and high chairs.
Alison Jacobson, executive director of the trade association the Baby Safety Alliance, said it is a great first start but other important items like cribs and strollers were left off the list.
“Families should have access to safe, compliant baby products at prices they can afford. They shouldn’t have to worry and make any sort of compensation for having safe products,” Jacobson contended.
The trade framework does not specify what the new tariffs will be or when they’ll start. Jacobson argued they are an unnecessary burden on American parents with newborn or young children during what should otherwise be a joyful time. Even before President Donald Trump’s tariffs, which have fluctuated from 30% to 145%, raising children in the U.S. was not cheap. The online resource BabyCenter estimates parents should expect to pay more than $20,000 in a baby’s first year, not including hospital bills.
Jacobson pointed out her association hears from parents every day asking about the safety of used baby items purchased online or handed down from family members. She advised saving a little money is not worth it.
“If there is a product that has been used before, it could have potentially been recalled. It may not meet standards, it might be counterfeit. And to have safe products for your family is literally a matter of life and death,” Jacobson emphasized.
She stressed baby products are highly regulated and it is important to look for the Baby Safety Alliance verification seal when buying online. The association’s website also includes lists of products meeting safety standards.
The Trump administration has previously suggested it may offer $5,000 “baby bonuses” to encourage American women to have more children, but Democratic lawmakers, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said families need much greater financial relief.

title: Maine’s remote Lobster Lake makes for an outstanding wilderness destination
text:
For several years, my son, Adam, and I have completed fall paddling and mountain hiking outings we call “surf and turf” trips. In the past, we’ve enjoyed surf and turf adventures on Moosehead and Tunk lakes, and Donnell and Attean ponds.
This year, we set our sights on Lobster Lake and Lobster Mountain. Located in a remote wilderness area northeast of Moosehead Lake, the exceptionally beautiful, pristine body of water is shaped something like a lobster, if you use your imagination.
Getting to Lobster Lake is not easy, and much of the journey is on dirt logging roads in northern Maine. Since Adam lives in West Forks, we started our trip there.
Initially, we drove north on Route 201 to Jackman and then east on Route 6 to dirt Demo Road on the left. From there, we traveled northerly on the often rough Demo and Northern roads to Seboomook Road near Pittston Farm. Our drive continued east on Seboomook Road along the south and east sides of Seboomook Lake and then north along the West Branch of the Penobscot River until arriving at a landing on Lobster Stream, close to where it enters the river from Lobster Lake. In all, our driving time was about three hours from West Forks and required passing through a North Maine Woods gate where road fees are collected.
We launched solo kayaks on the stream late morning on a partly cloudy day with cool temperatures and moderate southwest winds. The water was calm as we paddled south 2 miles to the lake. Shallow water at the entrance led us to conclude a minimal flow was being released from nearby Seboomook Dam on the West Branch which determines the water level on Lobster Lake and stream. The depth increased as we emerged onto the lake and began a 2-mile open crossing in a southeasterly direction toward Ogden Point with some wind-driven chop on the starboard.
Three campsites were seen as we rounded Ogden Point in a narrow channel with Big Island on our left. We entered lengthy Little Claw Cove and then turned abruptly right into Jackson Cove in search of a campsite situated near the beginning of the trail to Lobster Mountain.
Kayaking along the south shore of the cove, we found the substantial campsite with a large picnic table, fire ring and nearby outhouse. The expansive location had several good tent sites and the trailhead was just beyond. Since we were expecting early darkness and a cold night, we set up tents, organized gear and gathered firewood in advance of our hike.
There is no sign marking the beginning of the trail but a narrow clearing in the forest is the obvious entrance. After a short distance, we found a sign with an arrow stating “trail.” We soon encountered the first blue blaze as we hiked easily on a gradual incline in a mixed-hardwood and conifer forest.
Following a short mile, the trail steepened and we entered a sparse, scenic spruce forest. We continued steadily upward until arriving at the apparent highpoint where signs pointed left to Lobster Overlook and right to Moosehead Overlook. In my only visit six years ago, there was no sign or obvious trail to Moosehead Overlook.
We hiked a short distance to Lobster Overlook. This is an exceptional location that provides a panoramic vista of most of the lake. We studied the lake in anticipation of a circumnavigation the following day. A very narrow channel could be seen at the southern end of Little Claw that connects east to Big Claw. That would be part of our exploration.
The longer trek to Moosehead Overlook provided an unexpected treasure. From the west-facing viewpoint, we enjoyed extensive views of much of Moosehead Lake and the surrounding mountains. We reminisced about our surf and turf outing on Moosehead Lake a few years ago when we first learned that Little Mount Kineo is actually higher than Mount Kineo.
Our return to the campsite went smoothly and it was dark and cold by the time we finished dinner. The campfire kept us warm for a short time before retiring early in anticipation of some serious paddling the next day.
Read about more surf and turf adventures in my book “Maine Al Fresco: The Fifty Finest Outdoor Adventures in Maine.“
The author of “The Great Mars Hill Bank Robbery” and “Mountains for Mortals – New England,” Ron Chase resides in Topsham. His latest book, “Maine Al Fresco: The Fifty Finest Outdoor Adventures in Maine” is available at North Country Press and through online retailers. Visit his website at ronchaseoutdoors.com or he can be reached at [email protected].

South Portland schools to consider AI moratorium for grades pre-K through 8
text:
South Portland school board votes down AI moratorium for grades pre-K through 8
The South Portland Board of Education voted against banning students from using artificial intelligence for the rest of the school year.
South Portland school board votes down AI moratorium for grades pre-K through 8
The South Portland Board of Education voted against banning students from using artificial intelligence for the rest of the school year.
The South Portland Board of Education voted against a ban that would have prohibited students in grades pre-K through 8 from using generative artificial intelligence for the rest of the 2026-27 school year.
Many teachers who showed up for public comment on Monday night voiced concerns about losing essential parts of their curriculum if AI were to be banned, specifically computer science and STEM instructors. Some teachers also claimed they were not notified that the issue would be taken up at Monday night's meeting.
The South Portland School Department currently doesn't have a specific policy around AI, and officials say school staff also need to be given comprehensive training on the technology.
Some students who spoke cited AI-generated content as a hindrance to their learning.
"I deserve a right to a high quality education at this school, and that is being compromised by a certain teachers and curriculums in this school being generated with AI," said one student in favor of the ban.
The proposal also noted that the district doesn't have a full accounting of how widely generative AI is currently being used in classrooms. Earlier this year, a Pew Research Center survey found that 54% of adolescents aged 13 to 17 used A.I. chatbots to help them with schoolwork.
"I am very passionate about arming our children with the skills of how to think about AI and to teach our teachers how to use it ethically and responsibly," said a teacher opposed to the ban.
South Portland school officials have cited concerns about the impact generative AI can have on children's cognitive development, with several studies detailing links between the technology and worse learning, memory and social development outcomes. For now, there will be no change to AI usage in South Portland Public Schools.

title: Nvidia investigates whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese spy with whom he had an affair
text:
(AP) - Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company’s board of directors said Sunday.
The announcement came after Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom, according to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing.
In a letter to Nvidia employees obtained by The Associated Press, Huang said he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologized to his family and colleagues. He said he took “full responsibility” for his actions.
“Leading Nvidia is the privilege of my life,” Huang wrote. “My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility.”
Nvidia’s board said it has “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” the board said.
Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation.
“Today’s news will not slow Nvidia,” company spokesperson John Rizzo said in a statement. “Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption.”
Nvidia has become a central player in the global race to develop artificial intelligence, with its chips powering many of the data centers and computing systems used to train and run AI models. Its advanced processors have also been a focus of U.S. export restrictions aimed at limiting China’s access to cutting-edge semiconductor technology.
The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had discovered that Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. The two are not related, according to the Times.
Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to the Times.
The Nvidia CEO’s letter to employees did not name Alice Huang or address her apparent ties to Beijing. He did, however, refer to the national security concerns raised in news reports and said he supported the board’s investigation and would cooperate fully.
“I love our country and our company,” Jensen Huang said. “I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security.”
President Donald Trump said Sunday he hasn’t spoken to Huang about the latest development and praised him. “I hope everything’s fine then. He’s done such an incredible job,” Trump said, speaking to reporters before returning to the White House.
Asked whether he wished he had acted on intelligence when he was briefed about spying, Trump again praised Huang: “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. He’s done an amazing job for our country.”
As to whether he’d take the CEO with him on his trip to Asia next week, Trump said he was open to it.
“I don’t know, but I’d certainly take him,” he said of Huang, who serves on the president’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday as he was departing the U.S. for a G7 meeting in Paris that he could not address the situation with Huang.
“I just can’t comment because of the nature of it,” he told reporters. “And I also can’t comment on an internal corporate matter that’s going on with Nvidia.”
Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company, has regularly surpassed Wall Street’s earnings expectations in the past three years since its high-end chips emerged as AI’s best building blocks. The Santa Clara, California-based company reported quarterly profits of $59.69 billion in August.
___
Associated Press writer Michelle L. Price contributed to this report from West Palm Beach, Florida.
