title: Missing teen from Dixfield found safe, Sheriff's Office says
text:
Missing teen from Dixfield found safe, Oxford County Sheriff's Office says
The Oxford County Sheriff's Office says a Dixfield teen who was reported missing on Monday has been found safe.
Blake Brochu, 13, went missing at about 11:30 a.m. and had last been seen near Towle's Corner Store at the intersection of Weld and Main streets, according to authorities.
Shortly before 6 p.m., the Sheriff's Office announced that Blake had been located and is safe.

title: Rep. Thomas Massie forcing vote on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth impeachment
text:
Rep. Thomas Massie forcing vote on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth impeachment
Rep. Thomas Massie has drafted articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, which he plans to reintroduce in the House of Representatives this week.
Rep. Thomas Massie forcing vote on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth impeachment
Rep. Thomas Massie has drafted articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, which he plans to reintroduce in the House of Representatives this week.
Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) is moving to force a vote on articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
He introduced the 34-page resolution on the House floor Monday afternoon.
"In all of this, Secretary Hegseth has acted in a manner contrary to his trust as Secretary of Defense," Massie said on the House floor.
Massie has accused Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, arguing he continued unlawful military operations in Iran without congressional authorization.
Hegseth responded while talking to reporters on Monday:
“If you want to take issue with what we did in Epic Fury or Rough Rider or nabbing Nicolás Maduro, you’re taking issue with the troops and what they accomplished, which is historic."
He plans to hold a news conference at the Pentagon on Tuesday, his first in over 180 days.
President Trump has stayed supportive, telling 60 Minutes on Sunday he still has confidence in Hegseth.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he expects House Democrats to provide "incredibly strong" support for Massie’s effort.
"My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming when the Democrats assume control of the House and Senate next year," Massie said in a statement Monday. "They will hold hearings and trials. President Trump should replace Secretary Hegseth now while he can still get a replacement confirmed in the Senate."
A vote in the House could come by mid-week.
The articles
Provided by Massie via news release:
Article I - Waging War in Contravention of the War Powers Resolution of 1973 Section 2(c): Charges Secretary Hegseth with waging the Iran war despite no declaration of war, statutory authorization, attack on the United States, or imminent threat. It establishes that the war was unlawful from its inception.
Article II - Waging War in Contravention of the War Powers Resolution of 1973 Section 5(c): Charges Secretary Hegseth with continuing the Iran war after both Houses of Congress directed the removal of U.S. forces through H. Con. Res. 86. It focuses on his refusal to obey Congress’s express direction to terminate unauthorized hostilities.
Article III - Waging War in Contravention of the War Powers Resolution of 1973 Section 5(b): Charges Secretary Hegseth with continuing hostilities in Iran after expiration of the War Powers Resolution’s 60-day termination period and any potential 30-day withdrawal period. It establishes that he treated mandatory statutory deadlines as discretionary.
Article IV - Ignoring Laws that Minimize Civilian Casualties: Charges Secretary Hegseth with ignoring laws that minimize civilian casualties.
Article V - Extrajudicial Killings: Charges Secretary Hegseth with replacing maritime law enforcement with unauthorized lethal military targeting of suspected drug traffickers, resulting in at least 243 deaths. It also addresses denial of quarter, secondary strikes on survivors, failure to rescue shipwrecked persons, and the creation of artificial legal authorities for the campaign.
Article VI - Suppressing Free Speech: Charges Secretary Hegseth with using DOD authority to retaliate against and intimidate Senator Mark Kelly for constitutionally protected speech questioning unlawful military orders.
Article VII - Kidnapping of a Sovereign Foreign Leader: Charges Secretary Hegseth with directing Operation ABSOLUTE RESOLVE to seize Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores in Venezuela without constitutional or legal authority.
Article VIII - Unlawful War in Yemen: Charges Secretary Hegseth with initiating Operation ROUGH RIDER without congressional authorization or an imminent threat to the United States, while also violating war powers reporting requirements.
Massie is calling for his impeachment, removal from office and disqualification from holding federal office in the future.
The U.S. House of Representatives reconvened at noon Monday after being out of session since the beginning of October.
Since the resolution is privileged, House Speaker Mike Johnson has two legislative days to schedule a vote or action on the measure.
The House will vote on whether to impeach Hegseth. A simple majority is needed to pass the resolution. With the current numbers, a small number of GOP defectors plus full Democratic consensus would be enough to pass it.
If the House impeaches Hegseth, the articles move to the Senate. The Senate would then hear evidence and arguments from prosecutors (sitting representatives) appointed by the House.
To convict and remove Hegseth from office, the Senate needs a two-thirds supermajority vote, making removal unlikely unless a sizable group of Republicans turns on Hegseth and Trump.

title: Post-election and ‘free at last’
text:
Martin Luther King, Jr. once proclaimed, “Free at last, free at last, thank God Almighty, we are free at last.”
Following the resounding defeat of Republican candidates for various local, county, state and federal offices, in this year’s midterm elections, we are now “free” to heal the severe wounds inflicted upon this country by President Donald Trump and his enablers and, therefore, begin the long and rather difficult process of allowing justice and fair play to again govern America.
The road ahead — to find equitable solutions for wealth inequality, healthcare, housing and ample food supplies, to name a few of the important and vital areas — will be long and cumbersome. However, as a country, America must continue this necessary process until and after the 2028 elections, to ensure a steady movement of progress to be made.
But, now for the present, we are “Free at last …”
John Mishler
Harpswell

title: Sophomore standouts, and other takeaways from field hockey finals
text:
Our Communities. Our Teams. Our Future.
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone—because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s Go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
Cheverus remained on top, Nokomis returned after more than a decade away, and Foxcroft Academy put its dominance on display at the field hockey state championships Saturday.
Here are a few takeaways from a raw and rainy afternoon and evening at Edward Little High School:
STELLAR SOPHOMORES
Looking to form a Miss Maine Field Hockey watch list for 2028? You may want to start with players who were on the turf Saturday.
All three champions had second-year players playing central roles in their victories and showing an impressive array of talents.
In the Class A game, Brooke Brunelle — whose sister Sydney is a senior and Miss Maine finalist — was tenacious defending in the midfield and was one of the Stags’ fastest players getting the ball up the field.
She didn’t find the net, but she had an assist on freshman Avery Tinker’s goal, took the ball down the left side for a chance early in the fourth quarter and was a primary ball handler on corners.
In the B game, Maeve Rush of Nokomis dazzled with the ball on her stick. She was the Warriors’ most dangerous player in the open field, showed elimination skills to get around defenders, and had the vision and passing ability to find teammates on the attack.
“The biggest thing I’ve always noticed is the way that she can distribute the ball and her vision,” Nokomis coach Lauren Neal said. “That’s something that not everybody can get to, and having that automatically brings you to that next level.”
In Foxcroft’s 2-0 win in Class C, Addie Rayfield showed why she’s the Penobscot Valley Conference Player of the Year while potting a pair of goals, burying the second on a perfectly placed reverse that beat the goalie inside the right post while she was moving to her left.
“She’s an amazing player,” said senior Jenna Hartford, who assisted on both goals.
GAMER GOALIES
There were no blowouts Saturday, with each game decided by two or fewer goals. The goalies were a big reason why.
In the Class A game, Cheverus turned its pressure into 16 corners but only scored on one of them. Mt. Ararat goalie Jaymie Bergman was excellent (the Eagles’ book credited her for 18 saves). She used the space well in front of the cage to cut off angles, read the ball well through traffic, and got back to prevent Stags forwards from knocking in shots by the posts.
In the Class C nightcap, Foxcroft kept the play almost exclusively in the Winthrop/Maranacook end of the field, forcing netminder Cyara Harriman to keep the Ramblers in the game. She was up for the challenge, making eight saves while frequently batting and kicking balls away to steer traffic from the goal.
As a result, Winthrop kept the game scoreless for over 42 minutes, and kept alive its hopes of an eighth state title against the second-highest scoring team in state history.
DOESN’T HAVE TO BE PRETTY
Cheverus throughout the season showed a knack for the gritty goal, putting a long, bouncing shot toward the net and looking for a stick to deflect it in, or taking a shot on goal and crashing on the rebound to be the first ones to knock it home.
With players like Tinker (20 goals this season), Mary McCartney (16) and Jaylee Radford (13) up front, Cheverus often cashed in that way this fall, and became lethal on corners.
“You don’t get any points for style,” Cheverus coach Andrea Musante said.
Cheverus didn’t need the style points to take a 1-0 lead. Brooke Brunelle took a shot on a corner, with Tinker standing by Bergman awaiting a deflection. Bergman made the initial stop but lost her footing, and Tinker scrambled to the rebound and got the shot off before Bergman could get into position and scored off her pad.
THEY’LL BE BACK?
So what could the matchups next year look like? Well, with none of the teams that played Saturday being gutted by graduation, maybe pretty similar to this year’s.
In Class A, both Cheverus and Mt. Ararat are built well for next fall. The Stags, who have already proven their staying power with four straight undefeated seasons, graduate Sydney Brunelle, center midfielder Ava Martin and McCartney from their starting lineup, but bring back their backfield as well as three of their top five scorers.
Mt. Ararat loses Krystah Coen (the Eagles’ lone scorer Saturday) and Sarah Middleton in the backfield, and Maddy Sweet and Addison Chubbuck up top, but seven starters return and freshman Leah Lafrance is poised to become a top goal scorer in the state. Midfielder Kam Chase and center back Emma Graffam return as the Eagles’ backbone.
In Class B, Freeport was supposed to be rebuilding this year, and instead came within a goal of the state championship. Seven starters will be back, including top threats Dalila McCarthy and Ava Emmons, as well as goalie Lydia Costa.
Nokomis will say goodbye to midfielder MaKenzie Watson, perhaps its top all-around player Saturday, but seven starters, including Rush, impressive freshmen Ava Roundy and defensive standout Ella Toulouse ,are returning.
In Class C, Winthrop will see five starters leave, including two defenders and Harriman, but the Ramblers have shown their ability to contend year-in and year-out. And Foxcroft brings back seven starters, including Rayfield and freshmen Kaydiense Nelson and Lilah French, both of whom thrived on the championship stage. Nobody’s beaten the Ponies in two years, and it’s not going to get much easier.

title: Hall-Dale boys soccer completes state championship three-peat
text:
LEWISTON, Maine (WABI) - The Hall-Dale Bulldogs completed a Class C boys soccer state championship three-peat on Saturday in Lewiston.
Greyson Cary’s goal stood as the game-winner in the Bulldogs’ 1-0 victory over Fort Kent.
He spoke after the championship about what it’s taken this program to get here.
“Many of these guys, it’s their last game, so to be able to give them that win, it was the best feeling. We worked so hard for this the whole year. We go home, celebrate, this will probably kick in for the next week, and then from there, it’s working on the next one, No. 4,” said Cary, junior forward.
The Bulldogs’ current run encompasses all three of their state titles in team history.

title: Asian-style doughnut shop opens in Westbrook
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
A new doughnut shop featuring Asian-inspired flavors opened recently in Westbrook.
Donut Things Cafe launched at 113 Saco St. on Nov. 1, in the former space of Lucky Thai Variety.
The 12-seat shop sells specialty doughnut including pandan coconut crunch with palm sugar drizzle, matcha Oreo, matcha maple bacon, yuzu honey and vanilla jasmine. They also serve more standard doughnut and like classic glaze and chocolate, along with creative twists like the Biscoff Dragon with espresso-caramel drizzle.
Owner Sokly Soeuy said her brother, San, owned two doughnut shops in California until 2020, and trained her to make doughnut. Soeuy and her son, Ariya Chayarath, will run the shop.
The beverage menu includes coffee from Swift River Coffee Roasters in Raymond, matcha and other teas, and soft drinks like lemonade.
Donut Things Cafe is open Monday-Saturday from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m.

title: Windham quilt shop to close after more than 4 decades
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Calico Basket Quilt Shop in Windham is set to close permanently on Nov. 28, after over 40 years in business.
Neola Lussier, daughter of longtime store owner Jo-Anne Hill, said she took over the operations of the store earlier this year after putting her 90-year-old mother in a nursing home. Lussier said that her reason for closing the shop down was the stress of having to run the business while simultaneously caring for her mother and her house.
Lussier said the staff of the store, which consists of one remaining employee alongside her family and friends, are hard at work selling off the remaining inventory, and she was uncertain if they will have enough left to make it to Nov. 28.
Lussier spoke about Hill’s impact on her family. She said her mother is an expert in every aspect of making clothes, even making clothes for her children when they were young. Meanwhile, employee Kathy Larkin said that Calico Basket was the only quilt shop in Windham when it opened, and attracted dedicated customers, with Hill leading quilting classes for more than 40 years.
One of those customers, Grace Lund, who discovered the store earlier this year, said she loved the idea of a family-owned quilt shop in Windham, and is sad to see it go.
The store, located at 31 Page Road in Windham, is selling all items at 30% off. According to a Facebook post from Neola Lussier’s daughter, Shanice Lussier, Calico Basket Quilt Shop will be open from Wednesday through Saturday each week for the remainder of the month, save for Thanksgiving Day. The final day of sale will be Nov. 28.

title: Gold Scam Targeting Maine Seniors Ends With Nine-year Sentence For Indian National
text:
An Indian National has been sentenced in Maine for an elaborate scam that targeted residents of several states.
Indian National Sentenced in Maine for Multi-State Gold Scam
We've reported on this type of scam before, in which criminals prey on people's insecurities about their savings and investments.
The U.S. Attorney for Maine says Prakashkumar Prajapati, 47, was in a Maine courtroom last week after pleading guilty to conspiring to commit wire fraud.
READ MORE: Avoid These 16 Crimes That Can Happen to Anyone
Prajapati is sentenced to nine years in prison and ordered to pay $1,897,386 in restitution.
Court records state that Prajapati worked with others in a multi-state scheme to defraud at least eight victims in five states, including Maine.
Maine Victim Instructed to Buy Gold and Give It to a Fake Government Employee
The scam begins with victims receiving calls from people posing as government officials.
These imposters instruct the victims to withdraw cash from their accounts and buy gold with it, which the 'government' will hold for safekeeping.
The callers then tell victims that a government agent will meet with them so they can hand over the cash and the gold.
Prajapati's role in the scam was to direct his co-defendant, Bharat Awasarmol, to meet with victims to take their gold and money.
Awasarmol was intercepted when FBI agents caught him accepting a package from a victim in Maine.
That victim told authorities the caller had posed as a Federal Trade Commission employee.
Maine Courts Sentence an Indian National For a Multi-State Scam Targeting Elderly Mainers
In all, the conspiracy targeted victims in Maine, New Hampshire, New York, New Jersey, and Virginia.
Prajapati caused $1,897,386 in losses to his victims, money he has been ordered to repay.
Awasarmol pleaded guilty in December 2025 and faces up to 20 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000 for wire fraud conspiracy, and up to five years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000 for making a false statement.
If you or someone you know has been the victim of elder fraud, please call the National Elder Fraud Hotline at 833-FRAUD-11.

title: AI-generated political ads spiked in 2026, but campaigns still prioritized other means of messaging
text:
AI-generated political ads spiked in 2026, but campaigns still prioritized other means of messaging
For two election cycles, misinformation and election experts have wondered: Will content generated with artificial intelligence dominate races and mislead voters?
This story was originally published on PolitiFact.com.
Campaigns and their supporters still use conventional ads to try to influence voters. But there were more AI-generated ads in the 2026 midterms compared with the 2024 election.
And while this wasn’t “the ‘AI election’,” AI ads are the new normal, said Christina Walker, a University of Georgia international affairs assistant professor who studies how AI shapes political information.
About 300 political ads were generated or enhanced by AI this election cycle, according to analysis by the Wesleyan Media Project, which tracks and analyzes political advertising.
And the people and groups behind those ads spent about $187 million promoting them online and on TV, the Wesleyan Media Project said — more than 3,000 times the approximate $50,000 spent during the 2024 election cycle. But that’s still a fraction of the overall political ad spending, which ad tracking service AdImpact projected at about $11.6 billion in 2025 and 2026.
The Wesleyan Media Project said that about 90% of the ads it tracked came from Republican candidates or groups supporting them.
Why campaigns did not go all out with AI ads in 2026
There’s an AI learning curve for campaigns and it’s time-consuming for them to become comfortable enough with new technologies to ensure voters are OK with it too, said Travis Ridout, Wesleyan Media Project’s co-director, so there’s “reputational risk” to consider.
“You don’t want a voter backlash,” Ridout said.
Polls show that voters don’t necessarily want political content produced with AI. A 2025 Pew Research Center study found that 71% of Americans said they would like a candidate less if they knew the candidate used AI to help write a speech they had otherwise enjoyed.
“What people are okay with in terms of what AI is used for and how much it is used are still being worked out,” Walker said.
Many of the ads were essentially a “new medium for creating political cartoons,” said Tim Harper, who works at the Center for Democracy & Technology leading policy and advocacy work related to election disinformation.
Some AI ads fabricated information, others were more subtle
Some campaign ads included deepfakes, fabricated videos that appear to show people saying or doing something that they didn’t. Other ads used AI to enhance or supplement real incidents, such as adding more people to a video of a crowd.
Thirty-one states have laws regulating deepfakes in political messaging, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures. Those rules are being actively tested, Harper said.
Texas voters saw many ads with AI-generated visuals, including against state Rep. James Talarico, the Democratic candidate who won the state’s U.S. Senate race.
Campaigns also crafted and distributed their talking points in ways that made it likelier for AI chatbots to surface that information to voters who ask questions about candidates and election issues.
It’s difficult to gauge how much influence AI ads had on voters, who were inundated with many other messages on different platforms.
“AI content isn’t necessarily persuading audiences,” said Cayce Myers, a Virginia Tech public relations professor, but it’s confirming already held opinions.
AI still influenced voters, not because of the ways it helped produce political messaging, but based on concerns that the technology would lead to more data centers in their communities, depleting local resources, spiking energy bills and affecting their quality of life.
This story was originally published on PolitiFact.com.
It is republished here as part of a reporting and fact-checking partnership between PolitiFact and Hearst Television.

title: Who Is Jeremy Latcham, The New Head of DC Studios?
text:
Who Is Jeremy Latcham, the New Head of DC Studios?
The first question a lot of DC Comics fans have when they hear the news that James Gunn and Peter Safran are done at DC Studios and are being replaced is “Uhhhhhh what? Don’t they have another Superman movie coming out?”
(They do. Man of Tomorrow. It’s supposed to open in theaters on July 9, 2027.)
The second question is “Who is replacing them?”
That’s Jeremy Latcham, who will become the new president and chief creative officer of DC Studios. Although far from a household name, he’s a producer who does have a fair amount of superhero movie experience. He worked on a lot of the early films produced by Marvel Studios.
Latcham first joined Marvel back in 2004, and worked as a vice president of production and development in his time at the company. He eventually left Marvel in the late 2010s and founded his own production company. His projects since then include Bad Times at the El Royale and Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves.
At Marvel, Latcham served as an associate producer on Iron Man, a co-producer on Iron Man 2, and an executive producer on The Avengers, James Gunn’s Guardians of the Galaxy, Avengers: Age of Ultron, and Spider-Man: Homecoming.
READ MORE: Every DC Comics Movie, Ranked From Worst to Best
Here was Latcham’s statement on the news of his hiring to replace Gunn and Safran:
DC’s pantheon of characters is among the most iconic in American popular culture. I’ve had the privilege to help bring some of the most celebrated superhero stories to life on the big screen, and I’m excited and honored for the opportunity to now lead DC Studios into its next era. The chance to steward the incredible cast of DC characters to the screen in a way that excites lifelong fans while introducing their timeless stories to the next generation is a massive responsibility that I do not take lightly. I am grateful to Dana [Goldberg] and Josh [Greenstein] for putting their trust in me. I can’t wait to work night and day alongside filmmakers, comic book creators, artists and storytellers of every kind, across film, television and animation, to build something ambitious for longtime DC fans and newcomers alike.
One of the stranger aspects of Latcham’s job: His first movie as head of DC Studios will be Man of Tomorrow ... directed by James Gunn. The press tour for that film should be interesting!
The other key component of his hiring: What, if anything, he salvages from Gunn and Safran’s planned upcoming slate. When Gunn and Safran first took the jobs as DC CEOs, they announced ten interconnected movies and TV shows, most of which have yet to see the light of day. So that’s the next question: Will we ever see The Brave and the Bold or Swamp Thing or The People vs. Gorilla Grodd — a recently announced series for HBO Max that would have starred Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen? Gisondo originated the role in James Gunn’s Superman, so that could be a factor in its future as well.

title: US-led peace talks for Russia and Ukraine will look at security guarantees for both sides
text:
US-led peace talks for Russia and Ukraine will look at security guarantees for both sides
For the first time since February, Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. negotiators are scheduled to hold talks on ending the full-scale war that is nearing the five-year mark, with security guarantee stopping the agenda.
The two-day session starting Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, follows previous rounds of negotiations early this year that failed to produce any visible progress toward ending Europe’s most devastating conflict since World War II.
The negotiations follow last month's localized truce around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine that was brokered with the help of U.S. first lady Melania Trump and allowed the evacuation of some of its residents and the delivery of desperately needed humanitarian supplies.
But even as Moscow and Kyiv touted the weeklong ceasefire as a positive model, fierce fighting has continued along the 1,200-kilometer (about 750-mile) front line. Both sides also have escalated their long-range attacks on each other with drones and missiles.
Related video:
A look at the talks and what's on the agenda:
Russia and Ukraine have sharply divergent demands
Russia and Ukraine remain far apart on key elements of any prospective peace deal.
Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from the four regions that Moscow illegally annexed early in the war but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.
Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won't agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that such a pause would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects Putin’s demands to voluntarily cede Ukrainian territory Russia has not been able to take on the battlefield and agree to limits on the military and arrangements with Western partners, which it sees as essential security guarantees to stop Russia invading again in the future.
Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled.
Security guarantees top the agenda
Russia and Ukraine said the Abu Dhabi talks will focus on security guarantees.
Zelenskyy noted that Ukraine and its allies have discussed security guarantees similar to NATO’s Article 5, which states the alliance sees an attack on one of its members as an attack against all.
In an interview broadcast Nov. 5, he said Ukraine's security guarantees boil down to what Western allies would do if Russia launches a new invasion of his country.
“If Russia starts again, what will happen,” Zelenskyy asked. “Who will do what, with what means, and when?”
Some European nations have mulled a possible deployment of their troops to Ukraine after a prospective peace deal. Russia rejects that as a nonstarter, warning it would view any European troops on Ukrainian soil as legitimate targets.
The Kremlin insists that any prospective deal should offer security guarantees for Russia as well. Just before Moscow launched the all-out invasion in 2022, it demanded that NATO roll back its deployments of troops and weapons from the alliance's members in Central and Eastern Europe, seeing their presence as a security threat. Similar demands will likely be part of any comprehensive peace deal put forth by Russia.
U.S. President Donald Trump said after meeting Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House on Nov. 4 that some kind of grand deal about European security was in the works, although he did not elaborate.
“It’s going to be a big agreement and it’s going to involve more than Ukraine,” Trump said, adding that it might include all of Europe.
Ukraine wants Europe at the table but Russia says no
Ukraine insists its European allies must have a seat at the negotiating table, while Russia opposes any such involvement at this stage.
“No one is going to invite them to the negotiating table,” Kremlin foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov snapped when asked if European envoys could join the Abu Dhabi talks. He added that if they fly there, they won't be allowed into the room.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the Europeans would need to be involved in broader negotiations, but only later.
“Since the discussion will touch upon the future security architecture in Europe while addressing the mutual security of Russia and Ukraine, at some stage it would be impossible to do it without the Europeans,” he said.
On Oct. 27, Finland’s President Alexander Stubb and Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre spoke by phone with Putin in their first known direct conversation since shortly after the 2022 invasion. They said they spoke in their capacity as the heads of Russia's Nordic neighbors and not on behalf of the European Union, which has struggled to pick a negotiator with Moscow.
Peskov sarcastically noted that EU members “can’t even decide yet who is authorized to speak on their behalf,” calling it “a protracted indecisiveness and a lack of readiness on its part.”
On Nov. 4, Zelenskyy said in a post on X that he had held a 90-minute conversation with U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, saying the talks “must move forward at full throttle to bring this war to an end as quickly as possible.”
Kushner said on X that “our objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides, reduce the risk of future conflict, and create a more stable and predictable security environment.”
For over 30 years, “Europe and Russia have struggled to establish a sustainable security framework,” Kushner wrote. “Decades of mistrust, competing security concerns, and the devastating consequences of this war make this an extraordinarily difficult challenge, but one that is essential to lasting peace.”
He noted the main goals of the talks were “permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability.”
Russia’s envoy took a hard line at earlier talks
Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, who led Russia’s delegation in the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul in March 2022 and in subsequent sessions, remains Moscow’s chief negotiator.
A former culture minister who wrote books about purported Western plots against Russia over the centuries, Medinsky is known for his hard-line views and blustery statements. At the 2025 talks, also in Istanbul, he reportedly said it took Peter the Great 21 years to defeat Sweden in the 18th century and Moscow also is ready now to fight as long as it takes.
Russia ramps up strikes on Ukraine’s power grid
Putin has said repeatedly that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Ukraine fails to accept its conditions for peace.
Russia has intensified its strikes on Ukraine’s power system, seeking to undermine the country's resolve as winter sets in. Moscow has relied on ballistic missiles and new, faster jet-powered drones, taking advantage of Ukraine’s shortage of U.S.-made Patriot interceptors.
Zelenskyy said last week that “every power plant in Ukraine has been damaged in one way or another by attacks” and urged Kyiv's allies to provide generators and other equipment to keep the electricity flowing.
He also pleaded with allies to tap their own air defense stockpiles to help Ukraine fend off Russia's attacks and replenish them later.

title: FDA adds rare vision-loss warning to popular GLP-1 drugs
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Popular weight loss drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy will carry a new warning about a possible rare side effect that can sometimes lead to permanent vision loss, U.S. health regulators announced Monday.
The Food and Drug Administration said the risk will be added to the labeling of all GLP-1 drugs, the blockbuster medications used to treat obesity, diabetes and several other medical conditions. The class includes a dozen injectable or pill-based drugs, including widely used brands like Zepbound and Mounjaro.
The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss. The problem, which has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs, is caused by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve, although the underlying cause isn’t understood, the FDA said.
FDA scientists began looking into the problem after the publication of a 2024 medical paper tying the condition to certain patients taking semaglutide, the active drug in Eli Lilly’s Ozempic.
An FDA analysis of more than 125 clinical trials found that the problem occurred in roughly 6 of every 100,000 patients who took a GLP-1 for at least one year. The comparable rate for people taking a placebo or other types of glucose-lowering medications was less than 4 per 100,000, the FDA said.
The agency also found reports of the problem in its electronic reporting system for drug injuries and side effects.
Symptoms of the problem include blurred vision, blind spots, distorted colors and other visual disturbances, according to the FDA. Patients experiencing such problems should contact a health care professional immediately, the agency said.

title: Blood test could offer less invasive way to aid Alzheimer’s diagnosis
text:
(Aging Untold) — A familiar bike ride with her husband became frightening for Kathi Rigby when she suddenly struggled to communicate.
“I couldn’t get words from my brain to my mouth,” she said.
Rigby was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease in 2022. The news, she said, “was like a slap in the face.”
How the blood test works
Brain scans or tests of spinal fluid are often required to diagnose Alzheimer’s disease, but a blood test to detect amyloid plaque in the brain, a key marker of the disease, could offer a less invasive way.
In May 2025, the Food and Drug Administration cleared the Lumipulse, the first blood test cleared by the agency to aid in diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease.
“It’s a game changer. It’s indicated for people who are 55 years of age or greater with symptoms of cognitive decline,” Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician and Aging Untold host, said.
Researchers suggest that if a patient tests positive, there is a greater than 90% chance that they have amyloid plaque in their brain.
The FDA has cleared the blood test for use only in patients 55 and older who are already experiencing memory problems. The agency cautions that this is not intended as a standalone diagnostic tool for Alzheimer’s. Results should be interpreted alongside a patient’s medical history and other assessments, such as cognitive testing.
Why early evaluation matters
Rogers said identifying Alzheimer’s earlier can help people and their families plan and consider care options.
“I think it’s very welcoming because we know that like many diseases, especially Alzheimer’s, the earlier that you catch it, the more you can make an impact on quality of life,” she said.
For Rigby, early detection allowed her to participate in a clinical trial of a drug intended to remove brain plaque.
Her husband, Brent, said, “95% of the plaque was removed.” Rigby’s experience does not indicate how a treatment will work for someone else.
Rigby said the treatment made a difference for her.
“I want to be Grandma, and I want them to know that I love them—and I know them,” she said.

Russia's top independent newspaper closes its office after three decades, citing official pressure
text:
Russia's top independent newspaper closes its office after three decades, citing official pressure
Novaya Gazeta, Russia's most celebrated independent newspaper, closed its Moscow offices Monday, citing relentless pressure from government officials.
It was the last major independent media outlet critical of the Kremlin that remained active in Russia. Others closed or moved their operations abroad after President Vladimir Putin sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022.
In a statement published Oct. 30, the newspaper said the Russian authorities and the security services had "forced our editorial team to cease operations.”
Related video: Judge rules Trump administration must restore access for banned news outlets
“Human rights and freedoms have been abolished in this country, and defending them is now treated as a crime,” the newspaper said. "Elections and elected governing bodies have been effectively dismantled, civil society institutions have been wiped out, freedom of conscience and human dignity have been trampled underfoot.”
Launched in 1993, Novaya Gazeta quickly became known for its fierce reporting and dedication to uncovering Russian human rights abuses and corruption. Six of its journalists have been killed, including Anna Politkovskaya, who reported on atrocities during the second Chechen War at the start of Putin’s first term as president. She was fatally shot in her apartment building in 2006.
On the newspaper's final day in its office Monday, journalists slowly removed the portraits of their slain colleagues from the newsroom where reporters and editors planned their work.
Tatiana Britskaya, the editor of Novaya Gazeta's investigations desk, said she had expected the outlet's closure almost every day for the past 4 1/2 years.
“It is an incredibly difficult decision, because this is more than a workplace, more than an office — this is our home, and we're losing it,” she said.
Novaya Gazeta had faced growing government pressure as the Kremlin cracked down on critics, with repression sharply intensifying after the start of the conflict in Ukraine.
Longtime editor-in-chief Dmitry Muratov, who shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize with Philippine journalist Maria Ressa, was attacked on a train in 2022 by an assailant who poured red paint over him, causing severe irritation in his eyes. Muratov stepped down as editor in 2023 after being named a “foreign agent” by Russian authorities. The designation carries strong pejorative connotations in the country and can bring additional government scrutiny.
The newspaper was fined after it was accused of discrediting Russia’s armed forces, and it also was declared a foreign agent. Authorities blocked all of its online platforms, seized its printing house, revoked its media registration and shut down the donation system that allowed it to receive support from readers.
In a final blow, the newspaper was ordered to clear out its Moscow offices.
As reporters left the building and gathered in the street, a new sign was affixed atop the nameplate that once announced the newspaper's office. It read, “Here lived Novaya Gazeta.”
Sergei Sokolov, Novaya Gazeta's editor-in-chief, said he believed the newspaper would return one day “with renewed strength.”
“We will live, and I am sure that this country, caught in such a terrible era, will eventually stir. As soon as those first signs appear, Novaya Gazeta will return, to our readers and to our colleagues.”
Some of Novaya Gazeta’s staff left Russia in 2022 and opened a separate project, Novaya Gazeta Europe. The new outlet has been sharply critical of the Kremlin and its military action in Ukraine.

title: Trump says his deportation policy ‘might have been too tough’ for voters in the election
text:
(AP) - President Donald Trump in his first major interview since his party lost control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections said he thinks his administration was too aggressive on deportations and that he thinks he can work with Democrats in the new Congress on some kind of immigration deal.
Trump said his deportation policy was part of the reason Republicans lost, telling CBS’s “60 Minutes” in an interview that aired on Sunday: “I think it might be too tough, yeah.”
He added that he thinks he could reach an agreement with the new Democratic majority. “The deal would be we would work something out. And I think it’s something -- I think that’s something that’s actually doable,” he said in the interview.
Trump did not give specifics about what that deal would look like — and shortly after taping the interview on Friday, Trump named the key architect of his hard-line immigration agenda, Stephen Miller, as his new chief of staff.
“Trump says his immigration crackdown went too far,” Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer scoffed on social media Sunday after the interview aired. “Apparently, his solution was to put the man responsible for it in charge of the White House. That’s not a course correction. That’s a promotion.”
The president’s immigration crackdown was a prominent feature of his return to office with major operations in multiple cities sending arrests soaring. Two U.S. citizens — Renee Good and Alex Pretti — were killed by federal officers during protests against the operations.
Democrats have said oversight of Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Department of Homeland Security is a priority for the new Congress.
Trump said he believes that “killers” and “drug dealers” in the country illegally should be deported, but suggested he was open to the idea of a deal that would let others stay “if they’re good people working in a landscaping company, or working in a hotel, or doing something, right? And in some cases, paying taxes.”
Trump says he may stay on the sidelines for the 2028 race
On the race among Republicans to succeed him for the 2028 presidential election, Trump hinted at staying neutral.
Asked whether he’d endorse a potential successor, the president said “probably, not necessarily.”
“We have a tremendous bench. I have so many people that I have great relationships with,” Trump said in the interview.
Asked about possible candidates other than Vice President JD Vance, Trump only named Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is viewed as a possible 2028 contender.
“I think Marco’s great,” Trump said. “But there are many others and I’d rather not mention their names. There’s some senators that are excellent. I know ’em all, I like ’em a lot.
“So I may or may not get involved. I don’t know. Maybe I’m better off not getting involved,” Trump said.
Trump brushes aside questions about becoming wealthier while in office
During the midterms, Democrats sought to make the president’s personal wealth a campaign issue. About half of voters nationally said government corruption was “crucial” for their vote for Congress, according to the AP Voter Poll.
Asked how his net worth went up by $3 billion since returning to the White House, Trump said he doesn’t pay much attention to it and said his sons look after the family business.
“I devote almost no time to my net worth. I don’t care. I make — I have a lotta money, and far more than I ever thought I’d have. And I guess it’s gone up. I don’t even know,” he said.
Trump was asked whether he thinks people from foreign countries investing in the company he co-owns with his sons are trying to buy influence. “I don’t know. But that’s true — look, every president has a problem,” he said.
Trump, who survived an assassination attempt while campaigning for reelection in 2024 and has lashed out against his political foes, was asked whether he could forgive his enemies. He said it would be easy to say yes.
But he added: “I probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies, and I always will.”

title: South Portland approves city-funded curbside composting
text:
South Portland households will be able to choose to participate in a city-funded weekly curbside composting collection as early as July.
The South Portland City Council voted 4-3 to institute an opt-in curbside composting program on Nov. 5. The city’s rate of diversion from trash is expected to increase by 10% if 40% of households (or 3,600) participate, as estimated.
Households that opt in will be provided with a starter kit that includes a 5-gallon bucket, compostable liners and an information booklet or magnet. The vendor will empty the buckets each week, but will not provide clean ones (newspaper works as a liner).
The program will increase the average annual household taxes by $13, bringing the average property tax for waste management from $152 to $165. The city will pay for supplies and collection services only for the households that are proactively interested and more likely to participate, according to Sustainability Director Julie Rosenbach.
The program will provide a savings opportunity for the roughly 850 households that currently pay more than an additional $200 per year for a private compost collection service.
The decision came about two months after the council squashed a proposal to switch to city- issued, pay-as-you-throw trash bags because many said it would burden residents. Some residents and councilors worried that even the composting fee would be too much.
Councilor Carter Scott said that the change is comparatively low cost, and that the city needs to move forward with waste reduction solutions incrementally.
“We have to make some step forward,” she said.
Maine’s landfills are filling up, and municipal waste disposal costs are rising. The city’s costs are projected to increase by $188,000 — or about 10% — this fiscal year. With this option, tipping costs would be reduced by $48,000 (the program will ultimately cost the city $185,000 to fund annually, and $46,000 for the first year). Diverting waste from trash disposal could be a long-term cost-saving strategy, Mayor Elyse Tipton said.
Currently, about 20% of South Portland residents compost, redirecting about 400 tons of food waste annually, according to Rosenbach. About half are enrolled in Garbage to Garden’s curbside pickup, and the other half drop their compost off at the five free municipal collection sites. The city will retain three drop-off sites for overflow needs and for households that don’t opt in, saving the city $19,300.
The city will put out an RFP to find a suitable vendor.
Municipal staff predict that participation rates could more than double with the addition of a city-operated curbside composting program, and that food waste diversion would consequently double (from 5% to 10%).
Councilor Jessica Walker voted against the program because she didn’t think it went far enough. She said it costs too much for minimal waste reduction, and she recommended an ongoing conversation about different methods, including more community input.
Rosenbach said she didn’t think the city would be able to reduce organic waste in trash by 70% by 2030, a previously articulated goal, without curbside composting.

title: Russell Brand Sentenced to 10 Years in Jail
text:
Russell Brand Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison
Actor and comedian Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison. Last week, Brand was found guilty of four criminal acts, following a trial in London that lasted four weeks.
According to London’s Metropolitan Police, Brand “will be on the sex offenders’ register for life. Last week, a jury at the same court found him guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault following a four-week trial.”
One of Brand’s victims said in a statement “I am eternally grateful to the police and prosecution team for their support and for allowing my voice to be heard. I finally feel believed.”
READ MORE: The Best Movies of 2026 So Far
Brand, once one of the most popular comedians in England and then a film star around the world in projects like Forgetting Sarah Marshall and Get Him to the Greek, cultivated a comic persona as a wild (and often controversial) provocateur. In recent years, he had reinvented himself as a conservative YouTuber and podcaster.
In 2023, Channel 4 aired the documentary Russell Brand: In Plain Sight detailing allegations of Brand’s mistreatment of women. The police launched an investigation shortly thereafter, which eventually led to this trial and conviction.
“Brand's offending,” per the Metropolitan Police, “was between 2004 and 2009 and included one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women. The offences took place in different locations, including a radio station, the set of a DVD recording and Brand's home address.”
Brand had insisted on his innocence throughout the trial. Now he is going to prison. And according to The Independent, police are still investigating further allegations against the actor.

title: Former Celtics teammates Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum set to face off for first time
text:
PHILADELPHIA — Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum — once anchors of an NBA championship team in Boston — haven’t made time to talk since the trade that ended their working relationship.
The former Celtics teammates have certainly had opportunities to catch up since Brown was traded to the rival 76ers in July for Paul George and draft picks.
They just don’t want to — and Brown and Tatum sure don’t plan to make small talk when the Celtics play Tuesday night in Philadelphia in the first matchup between the top two teams in the Eastern Conference.
“There’s nothing to talk about,” Brown said Sunday in Chicago. “He’s on his side; I’m on my side. Both of us are trying to win. Nothing to talk about. Check the ball up.”
The trade has been a success for both teams. The 76ers. with Brown and LeBron James aboard, are 9-2 and tied with the Lakers for the best record in the NBA.
The Celtics have the second-best record in the East at 8-2.
“I think it should be fun,” Brown said. “Never let a good opportunity for our team to show what we’re made of. I’m looking forward to it. Two heavyweights in the East. Let’s get it.”
Both stars are well aware the headlines and social media posts for this one are well beyond how both teams are playing on the court, or even how the Celtics blew a 3-1 series lead to Philadelphia in last season’s playoffs.
“It’s another game on the schedule,” Tatum said Sunday in Milwaukee. “It’s nothing more than Celtics versus Sixers.”
As for potential chitchat, Tatum said he’s “not able to tell the future.”
The trade busted up one of the league’s most successful 1-2 punches, after Brown and Tatum helped carry the Celtics to the 2024 NBA title.
Tatum missed most of last season while recovering from an Achilles tendon tear that happened during the 2025 playoffs, meaning Brown had to carry even more of the load for Boston — and he wound up with career-best averages of 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists.
Brown and Tatum’s off-court relationship was dissected throughout NBA media circles, and the question of whether they were more frenemies than friends could have strained their effectiveness this season in Boston.
Brown also seemed to feel underappreciated, a perception that only deepened when the Celtics included him in trade talks with Milwaukee when Giannis Antetokounmpo was on the market.
The Celtics instead stunned the NBA when Brown — the 2024 NBA Finals MVP and a five-time All-Star — was sent to the 76ers. When Brown got the call that Boston had traded him, he threw his phone across the room.
Brown said last month there was “ no beef ” between himself and Tatum, even as their squabbles dragged into the season.
“There might be a little lamb chops and some gravy,” Brown said last month in response to a social media post. “He should stay ready at all times.”
Brown took issue with Tatum saying in a video on his YouTube channel that he was “just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world” by Brown’s trade to the Philadelphia.
Brown responded on his Instagram account with a baseball cap emoji. “Cap” is slang for something that is not true. Asked if he had any response, Tatum sighed in October before expressing his frustrations with the entire situation for several minutes.
Both players have spoken glowingly about how they grew and thrived together during their nine years as teammates.
But the relationship has evolved since the Celtics chose Tatum as the player they wanted to build around after trading Brown in what amounted to a move to cut one of the two players with $300 million contracts from the payroll.
“I don’t have any animosity or beef, or ill will towards him,” Tatum said. “I think the toughest part is since he’s not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or the conversations haven’t been enough about what we accomplished — all the games we won, winning a championship, how we’ve grown together. It’s turned into this drama type of thing.”
Who doesn’t love a little drama in the NBA?
The game streams on Peacock and no doubt cameras and reporters will crowd the court ahead of the game trying to glean any interactions between the two stars.
Then the ball goes up. Brown said his feelings are in check.
“As of now, I’ve got no emotion toward nothing,” Brown said in Chicago.
He’s focused on leading the 76ers into NBA championship contention and a 2-1 road trip did nothing to dim the soaring expectations set for the franchise.
There are more good times ahead for Brown.
And none of them involve Tatum.
“I’m looking forward to our growth,” Brown said, “and we’ll get there.”

title: Vintage photos capture Raoul’s Roadside Attraction in Portland
text:
Raoul’s Roadside Attraction was a beloved restaurant, pub and music venue at 865 Forest Ave. in Portland.
It was opened in 1984 by Russell Turner, who ran it for seven years and then sold it in 1991 to Stephen and Linda James. Two years later, it was sold again to Peyton Hurlin. The final owners of Raoul’s were Mike Stuart, Rick Glover and Tracey Knight, who took over in 1996. Raoul’s closed for good in October 1998.
A Facebook page is dedicated to the years Turner owned it, where old show lists and concert photos are posted.
For the 16 years it was open, Raoul’s was a beloved local hangout, in part because it was a prime live music venue with a capacity of about 300 people.
Acts that performed at Raoul’s include Richard Thompson, Throwing Muses, Gil Scott Heron, Susan Tedeschi, John Hiatt and dozens of other nationally touring and local acts.

title: FBI investigates 'suspected homicide' aboard cruise ship out of Texas
text:
Suspect in custody as FBI investigates a possible killing aboard a cruise ship out of Texas
The FBI is investigating a suspected homicide aboard a cruise ship that returned to port after departing from Texas, and a suspect is in custody, the agency said Monday.
The FBI did not say whether any charges had been filed. The name of the suspect was being withheld pending notification of the victim's family, the agency said on social platform X.
The MSC Seascape, which departed from Galveston, is a towering white vessel that has 2,270 cabins, more than 1,600 crew and can host nearly 5,900 guests, according to MSC Cruises' website.
"On reporting a guest incident aboard our ship, we were instructed by the authorities to return to the Port of Galveston," Natasha Fernandez, a spokesperson for MSC Cruises, said in a statement.
The company is cooperating with authorities and providing support to those impacted, she said.
The company said the vessel has resumed its voyage and left Galveston as of Monday afternoon.
MSC Seascape currently runs from Galveston to the Caribbean for five-and seven-night stays, according to the company's website. The ship switched from Miami to Galveston last November, according to a news release.
Homicide investigations on cruise ships are uncommon. Earlier this year, a teenager was charged with murder and aggravated sexual abuse in the death of his 18-year-old stepsister on a Carnival Cruise ship out of Florida.
"The FBI is the primary federal agency authorized to investigate potential crimes on the high seas," the bureau noted in a post on X.

title: Underwater hockey is growing one player at a time
text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (InvestigateTV) — Inside Green Bay’s Kroc Center, athletes from small towns around the region are joining together to play a sport you probably haven’t heard of: underwater hockey.
Peter Covach is president of the Green Bay Underwater Hockey Club.
“You’ve got a weighted puck, sits at the bottom of the pool, and it moves up and down the pool like soccer or hockey,” Covach said.
Molly Banks has been around the sport her entire life.
“My parents actually met playing the sport probably 30 years ago,” Banks said. “Our whole family’s just been kind of hockey nuts since then.”
The 24-year-old will represent the U.S. later this year in Turkey as a member of the elite U.S. women’s team and is trying to help grow the sport one player at a time.
“Every time it comes up it’s always kind of a lecture, like, ‘Oh yeah, people don’t know about it,’” Banks said. “Because it’s such a small sport, getting people into it young is really important to help the sport grow, so as much as we can get the youth interested, it’s awesome for the sport and it’s awesome for the kids.”
Adalind Meyer is an up-and-coming player with the Green Bay club.
“Underwater hockey’s pretty fun and also I get to go underwater and hold my breath for a long time,” Meyer said, explaining what she likes about the sport. “Being on a team, yeah and going underwater and flicking the puck very far.”
The group is hopeful others will join for some underwater excitement.
“Being able to keep an open mind with it, because once you break through and get comfortable, it really is so much fun,” Banks said.
Covach said team spirit is important in the sport.
“It’s probably the worst spectator sport in the world, you need to have goggles on, be in the water looking at the play as it’s happening,” Covach said. “All you need to do is have a swimsuit and be able to swim from back and forth from the end of the pool to the other side. We have the gear, we have the coaching — people can come into any practice, and we’ll show them the basics and hopefully they’ll continue to play with us.”
While the season typically runs during the winter months, Covach says people are always able to get more information by visiting the team’s Facebook page.

title: Our native Maine holly: A winter wonder
text:
I like to say that I live in a swamp. While that is not technically true, my backyard experiences seasonal flooding. The spring peepers can sound like they’re putting on a full symphony orchestra, and wildlife is abundant year-round. Lately, I’ve been noticing and appreciating a shrub in my backyard. Winterberry, otherwise known as Ilex verticillata, is a native Maine holly, and it loves wet feet.
If you’re like me, when you think of a holly plant, you picture an evergreen shrub with glossy, spiny leaves and red berries. Instead, our native holly is deciduous, meaning it drops its leaves. It has many common names, and can be called Canada holly, northern holly, and appropriately for me, swamp holly. The name I hear most often around here is winterberry, which references the bold red berries that cluster around the branches. The species epithet, “verticillata,” is Latin for “whorled.” This describes the small white flowers, and then berries, that circle the stem. While the berries form in the fall, it’s winter when they shine; their cherry color pops against the snow.

title: Actor Donnie Dunagan, original voice of Bambi in classic Disney film, dies at 92, reports say
text:
(Gray News) — Donnie Dunagan, who voiced young Bambi for the original 1942 Disney classic, has died. He was 92.
The Hollywood Reporter was the first to report the news.
Dunagan’s agents confirmed to Variety that he died Nov. 4 of lung cancer.
IMDb lists Dunagan as the voice of young Bambi in the film. The Guardian reports he was just 6 years old when he was chosen for the role.
In the film, adolescent Bambi was voiced by Hardie Albright.
Dunagan also appeared in other films including 1939’s “Son of Frankenstein.”
“Bambi” was his last role. He then enlisted in the U.S. Marines and served three tours in Vietnam. He retired as a major in 1977. For his service, he received a Bronze Star and three Purple Hearts.

title: China dismisses a spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign
text:
China dismisses a spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign
China denied on Monday there was a spy plot attempt to ensnare Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the spying allegations unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against Beijing.
Huang has acknowledged to the Nvidia board that he had been intimate with a business executive who U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, according to The New York Times.
“The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China,” Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday.
Related video: How are President Trump's tariff policies affecting businesses?
Also on Monday, Nvidia shares dropped roughly 5% in pre-market trading.
The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies. Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft.
Nvidia said on Sunday that the company would launch an investigation into the case. Huang did not name the person in the extramarital affair.
China had previously denied the New York Times report that said Huang had developed a close relationship with a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, who ran a company that faced claims of smuggling advanced chips into China, and that she was a spy for Beijing.
“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.
“Those questions require evidence rather than speculation,” he added in a text message to reporters.
Huang had pushed to loosen chip sales restrictions to China in recent years, successfully lobbying U.S. President Donald Trump to allow his company to sell H200 chips this year. However, it is uncertain if Beijing would allow Chinese companies to buy these chips en masse. Nvidia said in a filing in August that it sold only a small amount to China as such sales are restricted by the Chinese government.
While those chips are not Nvidia's most cutting-edge models, they are still advanced. Previously, Huang also lobbied Trump to sell the less-advanced H20 chips, which were designed for the Chinese market while complying with U.S. export restrictions.
Chinese media have largely focused on Huang admitting to the affair and state media outlets have mainly echoed the official government line. Some have said the New York Times report was aimed at destabilizing U.S.-China relations.
“Whenever China-US relations begin to improve, there are often those firing shots from the shadows,” the state-owned Global Times said.
___

title: Three new Bangor city councilors sworn in; Daniel Carson elected chair
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - Three new Bangor city councilors took their seats this morning, bringing new perspectives on development, homelessness, and property taxes. The council also chose a new chair as well.
Terry Dinkins, Anthony Cote and Joseph Pratt took their oaths of office Monday morning as the three newest members of the Bangor City Council, filling the seats held by Susan Deane, Carolyn Fish and Joe Leonard.
“I think the voters in Bangor spoke loud and clear on a few issues. Homelessness, the city’s approach to homelessness, maybe the city’s approach to property tax,” said Pratt.
Leading up to the election on November 3rd, Dinkins, Cote and Pratt were all part of a conservative slate endorsed by the Concerned Citizens of Bangor PAC. All three new councilors say they’re eager to collaborate on the city’s direction.
“I just want to have communication between developers and people that want to invest in Bangor. Give them a place to express their concerns and what’s holding them back,” said Cote.
“I’ve been working with the homeless for 15 years, but I think we can help them to get off the streets. One of the things I see a lot is severe mental illness on our streets. I know we have to work with the state legislation and the representatives in the State Senate. I think we can make a difference for the mentally ill,” said Dinkins.
The results in the council election bucked the “Blue Wave” trend in other state and nationwide races.
“I don’t really see it as a divergence. If you look at it in terms of liberal conservative, I guess I see the contrast, but I don’t look at the Bangor election as a liberal-conservative election,” said Pratt. “I see it as a ‘common sense election.’ It’s very much consistent with what happened in the rest of the country.”
Daniel Carson and Susan Faloon both ran to be the new city council chair. The council elected Carson by a 7 to 2 vote.
“I’m really big on building relationships, so that’s with counselors, with the community. I think it’s really important that because we work together, we ought to know what things are important to each of us and each of our councilors. And so, I’m just going to continue to do that work that I was doing before, but as a chair,” said Carson.

title: Cruise ship pianist who fell overboard rescued from ‘middle of the ocean’ after 9 hours
text:
NEWPORT BEACH, Calif. (KCAL/KCBS) - Two fisherman helped save a Royal Caribbean pianist who fell overboard on a cruise ship then spent nine hours floating in the ocean nearly 20 miles off the California coast.
Sean Norton and Grant Garrett were headed back to Newport Beach after a Friday morning fishing trip when suddenly, their boat captain noticed someone in the water nearly 20 miles off the coast.
“I mean, it’s surreal,” Norton said. “Grant and I each got an arm and lifted him up, and he was in total shock.”
Garrett said when the 37-year-old man came to, he told them he’s a pianist on the 14-deck Royal Caribbean cruise ship called the “Ovation of the Seas,” which was en route to Ensenada, Mexico, out of Long Beach.
“The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,’” Norton said.
After pulling the man from the water, the crew put out an emergency maritime call, and a group of Newport Beach lifeguards responded to help.
“It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean,” Lifeguard Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda said.
Lifeguard officials believe the man went overboard around 2:30 a.m. Friday, roughly nine hours before he was found. He was hospitalized but is expected to survive, according to the U.S. Coast Guard, which is investigating the incident and how he went overboard.
“You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water’s 76 degrees. A different year, no way he makes it,” Norton said.
The fishermen are grateful they found the man and were able to help him.
“I’m glad we were there, and I’m glad he’s doing okay,” Garrett said.
A Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson released the following statement regarding the incident: “We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share.”

title: Ring camera video shows women making racist gestures outside Ole Miss student’s apartment
text:
OXFORD, Miss. (WMC/Gray News) - A disturbing video circulating on social media is drawing attention across the Ole Miss campus after women were caught on a Ring doorbell camera making racist gestures outside an apartment where three Black students live.
The video belongs to the daughter of Tasha Bolton, who contacted WMC about the clip.
Bolton’s daughter is an African-American freshman at the University of Mississippi. She shares the off-campus apartment with two other Black roommates.
What the video shows
In the video, three white women can be seen walking past the apartment’s front door. As they pass, two of the women appear to make monkey noises.
The video went viral Saturday after being shared on social media, prompting reactions from students and visitors in Oxford.
Reaction from students and visitors
Sophomore Olivia Landgreve, who does not live at the apartment, said she was upset by what she saw.
“I like to think that people don’t see me like that. I’m just a person like everybody else is. Very upsetting to think that maybe people are thinking other things while they’re looking at me while I walk on campus,” Landgreve said.
Landgreve said she had never experienced anything like this before and was shocked by the video.
Jamie Purcell, who was visiting Oxford from California, had not seen the video until WMC showed it to her.
“It’s disgusting and they’re just not smart, and they’re acting incorrectly to something people should know differently about,” Purcell said.
University statement
On Sunday, the University of Mississippi released a statement condemning the behavior.
“The university is aware of a video depicting offensive, hurtful, and unacceptable behaviors that conflict with our university values and we condemn them. The university has reached out to those targeted by the actions to share information, resources, and support.
“The incident is actively being investigated by the appropriate university offices and processes. It’s important to note that student conduct cases, records, and any potential disciplinary action are protected by the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA).
“We are committed to maintaining a safe and welcoming environment for all of our students, faculty, staff, and visitors and will follow our processes to ensure the well-being and safety of our community.”
Landgreve said seeing the incident was especially upsetting because of the progress she believes the university has made.
“It just kind of upset me a little bit because I feel like the campus has grown so much progress and just seeing things set us back like that is very upsetting,” Landgreve said.
Bolton, who shared the video, does not want to speak with WMC until she has had an opportunity to speak with the university.

Some of these athletes helped their teams reach regional and state championships. Others delivered strong individual performances or played important roles in their programs throughout the season.
All have earned recognition from the Aroostook League.
Congratulations to every athlete selected, along with the coaches, teammates and families who supported them throughout the fall.
And to all the seniors receiving these honors, congratulations on closing out your fall high school sports careers with All-Aroostook recognition.

title: Van Buren fire victim identified; fire classified as accidental
text:
VAN BUREN, Maine (WAGM) - A fire late Sunday afternoon, Nov. 8, 2026, at 128 Roosevelt Ave. in Van Buren started on the stovetop in the kitchen of Unit 207 and is classified as accidental. The injured woman has been identified as Cynthia Loux, 73.
The fire involved a 16-unit residential apartment building. The Maine Office of State Fire Marshal is investigating.
Sprinkler system contained fire
Firefighters responding to the scene found a fire in one of the apartment units. The building’s automatic sprinkler system activated and contained the fire to a single unit. The fire did not spread to other areas of the building.
Woman flown to Portland
Loux was found inside the fire-damaged apartment. She was taken to a local hospital and then transferred by LifeFlight to Maine Medical Center in Portland for further treatment.
She sustained serious injuries, including burns covering about 40 percent of her body and smoke inhalation.
Investigation
Investigators from the Maine Office of State Fire Marshal were scheduled to return to the scene Monday, Nov. 9, for a more detailed examination to determine the origin and cause.
The Maine Office of State Fire Marshal said automatic fire sprinkler systems are important in residential buildings. In this fire, the sprinkler system helped contain the fire to a single apartment and kept it from spreading throughout the building.
Additional information will be released as it becomes available.
